meta.title: Aurendel
meta.author: DungeonMaster
meta.description: A continent, and nothing else. Twelve regions from the Frostmere ice to the Glasslands, four cities, twelve towns, twenty villages, and the roads between them — with every shop, house, shrine, barrow, cave and castle you can walk into. No quests, no people, no loot: the geography is the whole of it, waiting for somebody to put a story in. Built on the Core Fantasy ruleset.

attributes.name: Might
attributes.description: Raw physical force: what you can lift, break, and hit with.

attributes.name: Agility
attributes.description: Speed, balance, and hands that do what you tell them.

attributes.name: Endurance
attributes.description: How much the world can take out of you before you stop.

attributes.name: Intellect
attributes.description: Learning, reasoning, and the memory to hold a long thought.

attributes.name: Instinct
attributes.description: What you notice without being told, and what you feel about it.

attributes.name: Presence
attributes.description: The weight you carry in a room, and your grip on your own nerve.

resources.name: Hit Points
resources.description: What is left between you and the end of the story.

resources.name: Focus
resources.description: Concentration spent on the difficult thing rather than the ordinary one.

derivedStats.name: Guard
derivedStats.description: How hard you are to land a blow on.

derivedStats.name: Initiative
derivedStats.description: Who moves first when it starts.

derivedStats.name: Carry
derivedStats.description: What you can haul before it starts to matter.

damageTypes.name: Cold
damageTypes.description: The heat taken out of a thing.

conditions.name: Bleeding
conditions.description: An open wound that has not been seen to.

conditions.name: Burning
conditions.description: Alight, and not going out on its own.

conditions.name: Poisoned
conditions.description: Something in the blood that should not be there.

conditions.name: Frightened
conditions.description: Nerve gone, and the body arguing for the door.

conditions.name: Emboldened
conditions.description: Steadied, and standing a little straighter for it.

conditions.name: Blinded
conditions.description: Sight gone, whether from dark, dazzle, or injury.

conditions.name: Slowed
conditions.description: Every movement costs more than it should.

conditions.name: Stunned
conditions.description: Nothing gets through for a moment.

conditions.name: Prone
conditions.description: On the ground, and everyone above you knows it.

savingThrows.name: Fortitude
savingThrows.description: Enduring what the body must endure.

savingThrows.name: Reflex
savingThrows.description: Being somewhere else when it lands.

savingThrows.name: Will
savingThrows.description: Holding your own mind against something that wants it.

actionTypes.name: Action
actionTypes.description: The one substantial thing you do in a turn.

actionTypes.name: Quick Action
actionTypes.description: Something done in the same breath as the main thing.

actionTypes.name: Reaction
actionTypes.description: Spent out of turn, on somebody else's mistake.

actionTypes.name: Speech
actionTypes.description: Talking costs nothing but the breath.

actionTypes.name: Gesture
actionTypes.description: A sign, a point, a hand held up.

itemProperties.name: Silvered
itemProperties.description: Chased with silver along the edge. Old things feel it.

itemProperties.name: Two-Handed
itemProperties.description: Needs both hands, and gives up the shield to get them.

itemProperties.name: Finesse
itemProperties.description: Rewards a quick hand over a heavy one.

itemProperties.name: Thrown
itemProperties.description: Meant to leave your hand and be regretted at a distance.

itemProperties.name: Heavy
itemProperties.description: Slow to bring round, and worth it when it lands.

itemProperties.name: Reach
itemProperties.description: Keeps them a step further away than they would like.

creatureTypes.name: Beast
creatureTypes.description: Things that hunt because they are hungry.

creatureTypes.name: Construct
creatureTypes.description: Made things that were given a purpose and kept it.

creatureTypes.name: Elemental
creatureTypes.description: Fire, stone, storm, and flood, given a shape and a temper.

creatureTypes.name: Fey
creatureTypes.description: Old, courteous, and not remotely safe.

creatureTypes.name: Giant
creatureTypes.description: Large enough that the ground remembers them.

creatureTypes.name: Dragon
creatureTypes.description: Winged, scaled, and older than the roads.

creatureTypes.name: Aberration
creatureTypes.description: Shapes that do not belong to this world's grammar.

creatureTypes.name: Plant
creatureTypes.description: What grows, and sometimes reaches back.

languages.name: Common
languages.description: The trade tongue of the roads and the ports.

languages.name: The Old Tongue
languages.description: What was written before the roads were cut.

languages.name: Delving Cant
languages.description: The clipped speech of the deep holds, half of it struck on stone.

languages.name: Sylvan
languages.description: The forest speech. Nobody agrees on how many words it has.

languages.name: Steppe Tongue
languages.description: Carried by riders, and by nobody who stays put.

languages.name: Glass Script
languages.description: A southern script, cut rather than written.

rests.name: Breather
rests.description: An hour sat down, out of the wind.

rests.name: Make Camp
rests.description: A fire, a watch rota, and eight hours of not walking.

rests.name: Take a Room
rests.description: A bed with a roof over it. Nothing interrupts a paid bed.

senses.name: Sight
senses.description: What you can see, which is nothing at all through a wall. Either something is in view or it is not, so every threshold is the same.

senses.name: Hearing
senses.description: Sound travels in a straight line and stops at stone, but passes an open doorway perfectly well. It fades with distance, so a far-off clatter is worth walking towards and a near one is worth drawing steel for.

senses.name: Smell
senses.description: Scent seeps around corners and hangs about long after you have gone. A hound follows where you went rather than where you are, and a cold trail is faint even underfoot.

stances.name: Sneak
stances.description: Slow and careful. Half pace, a fifth the noise, and rather less of your smell on the wind.

stances.name: Walk
stances.description: An ordinary pace. Nothing gained, nothing given away.

stances.name: Dash
stances.description: Quick, and heard from a long way off.

opportunities.name: Parting Blow
opportunities.description: Anyone who walks out of your reach gives you one free swing, which is what makes disengaging a decision rather than a formality.

skills.name: Athletics
skills.description: Climbing, swimming, forcing, and holding on.

skills.name: Stealth
skills.description: Moving without being heard. Ranks quieten a careful step further; nothing makes you silent outright.

skills.name: Lockpicking
skills.description: Locks, latches, and the small mechanisms of other people's privacy.

skills.name: Craft
skills.description: Joining, shaping, and repairing with the right tool in hand.

skills.name: Survival
skills.description: Tracks, weather, water, and which way is out.

skills.name: Perception
skills.description: Noticing the thing that was not meant to be noticed.

skills.name: Insight
skills.description: Reading a face for what it is not saying.

skills.name: Medicine
skills.description: Wounds, fevers, and knowing when to stop trying.

skills.name: Lore
skills.description: History, heraldry, and what the old books actually said.

skills.name: Arcana
skills.description: Wards, runes, and the shape of a working.

skills.name: Nature
skills.description: Beasts, growing things, and the habits of both.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.description: Getting a yes out of someone who began with no.

skills.name: Resolve
skills.description: Holding your nerve when the situation stops being reasonable.

abilities.name: Strike
abilities.description: A swing with whatever you are holding.

abilities.name: Quick Shot
abilities.description: A shot loosed before the target has finished deciding.

abilities.name: Guarded Stance
abilities.description: Give up the initiative and keep the ribs.

abilities.name: Rally
abilities.description: A word at the right moment, worth more than a shield.

abilities.name: Shove
abilities.description: Put them on the ground and take the second you bought.

abilities.name: First Aid
abilities.description: Pressure, a clean strip of cloth, and a hand that does not shake.

abilities.name: Read Runes
abilities.description: An hour with a hand on the carving, and it gives up its sense.

abilities.name: Wardlight
abilities.description: A cold light that clings to the one who holds it.

abilities.name: Frost Lance
abilities.description: A line of cold, drawn straight through whatever is standing in it.

abilities.name: Mend Flesh
abilities.description: The wound closes, though it will still want telling about later.

abilities.name: Turn the Dark
abilities.description: Named aloud, the old cold gives ground.

abilities.name: Augury
abilities.description: An hour of quiet and the right question, and something answers.

ancestries.name: Human
ancestries.description: Everywhere, adaptable, and short-lived enough to be in a hurry about it.

ancestries.name: Dwarf
ancestries.description: Hold-born. They measure a thing in centuries and are rarely wrong about stone.

ancestries.name: Elf
ancestries.description: Wood-kin and ruin-keepers. Long memories, longer grudges.

ancestries.name: Halfling
ancestries.description: Small, unhurried, and very hard to catch.

ancestries.name: Orc
ancestries.description: Steppe-bred and hold-broken both. Reputation runs ahead of them and is usually wrong.

classes.name: Warden
classes.description: Trained to hold a line, a bridge, or a doorway, and to be the last one through it.

classes.name: Stalker
classes.description: Roads, roofs, and other people's locks. Prefers the fight that never starts.

classes.name: Ranger
classes.description: Between the settlements, where the roads stop being roads.

classes.name: Adept
classes.description: A scholar of workings. Fewer bones than the others and rather more books.

classes.name: Keeper
classes.description: Tends the shrines on the road and what walks between them.

traps.name: Snare
traps.description: A noose in a run, set by somebody who knew which run.

traps.name: Covered Pit
traps.description: Hurdles and turf over a hole somebody took real trouble digging.

traps.name: Dart Slab
traps.description: A floor slab on a pivot, and a row of holes in the wall opposite.

traps.name: Falling Block
traps.description: A ceiling stone held by a pin, and the pin is on a trip.

traps.name: Scything Blade
traps.description: Set in a slot cut across the passage, and the slot has been swept.

traps.name: Broken Seal
traps.description: A jar bedded in the floor with a thread across the passage above it.

traps.name: Flame Jet
traps.description: A nozzle low in the wall, sooted in a fan across the floor.

traps.name: False Floor
traps.description: Snow-bridge over a melt hole, and it has held so far.

traps.name: Collapsing Stair
traps.description: Three treads rotted through and dressed to look like the rest.

traps.name: Alarm Wire
traps.description: A wire at ankle height with something noisy on the far end of it.

terrains.name: Grass
terrains.description: Ordinary turf, cropped short by whatever grazes here.

terrains.name: Meadow
terrains.description: Long grass and flowering weeds, up to the knee.

terrains.name: Cropland
terrains.description: Planted rows. Walking through them is nobody's favourite.

terrains.name: Fallow Field
terrains.description: Turned earth resting a season.

terrains.name: Mossy Ground
terrains.description: Deep moss over old roots. Quiet underfoot.

terrains.name: Leaf Litter
terrains.description: Years of leaf-fall, and it announces every step.

terrains.name: Heather
terrains.description: Woody purple scrub that hides the ground it grows on.

terrains.name: Steppe Grass
terrains.description: Grass to the horizon, all of it leaning the same way.

terrains.name: Shingle
terrains.description: Wave-rolled stones that slide underfoot.

terrains.name: Salt Flat
terrains.description: White crust over old sea-bed. It crunches.

terrains.name: Dirt Road
terrains.description: Rutted track, and better than the field beside it.

terrains.name: The Kingsroad
terrains.description: Cut stone laid straight, kept up by the crown and its tolls.

terrains.name: Cobbles
terrains.description: Round stones set in sand. Cart-ruts worn into them.

terrains.name: Flagstones
terrains.description: Flat-cut paving, the mark of somewhere that had money.

terrains.name: Boardwalk
terrains.description: Planks over water or mud, with gaps to watch for.

terrains.name: Timber Floor
terrains.description: Swept boards.

terrains.name: Rug
terrains.description: Woven and much walked on.

terrains.name: Bridge
terrains.description: A crossing with rails, or without.

terrains.name: Jetty
terrains.description: Boards on piles, out over the water.

terrains.name: Stair
terrains.description: Cut steps, going up or down as the case may be.

terrains.name: Shallows
terrains.description: Ankle-deep and cold.

terrains.name: Deep Water
terrains.description: Over your head. You will have to swim it.

terrains.name: River
terrains.description: Moving water with an opinion about where you are going.

terrains.name: Marsh
terrains.description: Standing water and sucking mud in equal measure.

terrains.name: Reeds
terrains.description: Tall enough to hide a person, and often does.

terrains.name: Bog Pool
terrains.description: Black water of no honest depth.

terrains.name: Tree
terrains.description: Trunk enough to stop you and shade enough to hide what is behind it.

terrains.name: Thicket
terrains.description: Young growth packed tight. Slow, and blind.

terrains.name: Bramble
terrains.description: Thorns that take payment in cloth and skin.

terrains.name: Stump
terrains.description: Cut a long time ago by somebody who is not here.

terrains.name: Rock
terrains.description: Bare stone, gone vertical.

terrains.name: Scree
terrains.description: Loose slope that moves when you do.

terrains.name: Cliff
terrains.description: You would need hands and a great deal of confidence.

terrains.name: Rubble
terrains.description: What a wall becomes.

terrains.name: Standing Stone
terrains.description: Raised by somebody, for some reason, and still standing.

terrains.name: Snow
terrains.description: Knee-deep in the drifts and shin-deep everywhere else.

terrains.name: Ice
terrains.description: Blue-white and unsympathetic.

terrains.name: Ice Wall
terrains.description: Glacier, sheared flat, older than any road.

terrains.name: Crevasse
terrains.description: A blue slot in the ice, and no bottom to see.

terrains.name: Ash
terrains.description: Grey drift that takes a footprint and keeps it.

terrains.name: Cinder
terrains.description: Black grit still warm from below.

terrains.name: Lava
terrains.description: No.

terrains.name: Steam Vent
terrains.description: A crack that breathes out, on its own schedule.

terrains.name: Obsidian Shelf
terrains.description: Black glass in sheets, and every edge of it is an edge.

terrains.name: Sand
terrains.description: Fine, pale, and everywhere afterwards.

terrains.name: Dune
terrains.description: A slope that resets itself while you climb it.

terrains.name: Glass Crust
terrains.description: Fused sand in fragile sheets. It sings when it breaks.

terrains.name: Cave Floor
terrains.description: Dry stone, worn smooth in the middle where things walk.

terrains.name: Cave Wall
terrains.description: Living rock.

terrains.name: Fungal Growth
terrains.description: Cap-forest to the shoulder, and it glows enough to see by.

terrains.name: Chasm
terrains.description: The floor stops. Something below it does not.

terrains.name: Stone Wall
terrains.description: Dressed block, or field-stone and mortar.

terrains.name: Timber Wall
terrains.description: Frame and daub, or plank on plank.

terrains.name: Mudbrick Wall
terrains.description: Sun-dried brick, whitewashed against the glare.

terrains.name: Hull Timber
terrains.description: Ship's planking, put to a second use ashore.

terrains.name: Door
terrains.description: Shut, but not necessarily against you.

terrains.name: Gate Arch
terrains.description: The way through a wall, when somebody is minded to let you.

terrains.name: Portcullis
terrains.description: Down, and going nowhere while it is.

terrains.name: Fence
terrains.description: Waist-high, and worth crouching behind.

terrains.name: Hedgerow
terrains.description: Centuries of laid thorn. A wall that grew.

terrains.name: Palisade
terrains.description: Sharpened stakes, set close.

terrains.name: Hearth
terrains.description: Banked, and the warmest thing for a mile.

terrains.name: Brazier
terrains.description: Coals in an iron basket, on a stand.

terrains.name: Table
terrains.description: Scarred, and bolted down in the rougher places.

terrains.name: Counter
terrains.description: The line between the customer and the stock.

terrains.name: Shelving
terrains.description: Floor to ceiling, and not quite full.

terrains.name: Barrel
terrains.description: Stood on end, and used as a table by whoever got there first.

terrains.name: Crate
terrains.description: Stencilled with a mark you would need the ledger to read.

terrains.name: Bed
terrains.description: Straw tick on a rope frame. It has known worse guests.

terrains.name: Anvil
terrains.description: Horn, face, and a hardy hole worn oval.

terrains.name: Loom
terrains.description: Warp-weighted, and taller than the weaver.

terrains.name: Pillar
terrains.description: Holding up more than it looks like it should.

terrains.name: Altar
terrains.description: Stone, worn pale in the middle by hands.

terrains.name: Urn
terrains.description: Waist-high, glazed, and sealed with wax.

terrains.name: Well
terrains.description: Wall, windlass, and a very long rope.

terrains.name: Market Stall
terrains.description: Trestle and awning, struck every evening.

terrains.name: Cart
terrains.description: Shafts down, tail-gate open.

biomes.name: The Kingsvale
biomes.description: River-country: hedged fields, mill-leats, and a road somebody keeps up.

biomes.name: The Silver Coast
biomes.description: Chalk over grey water. Wind off the sea and salt in everything.

biomes.name: Duskwood
biomes.description: Trees older than the kingdom, standing over what the kingdom replaced.

biomes.name: The Skarnspine
biomes.description: Cut passes, thin air, and stone that was worked long before anyone asked.

biomes.name: The Frostmere Waste
biomes.description: Ice with a grain to it, and a shoreline that the sea gave up on.

biomes.name: The Weeping Moor
biomes.description: Heather to the skyline, and under it more graves than living people.

biomes.name: The Ember Reach
biomes.description: Ash-fall country. The ground is warm and the weather comes from below.

biomes.name: Thornmere
biomes.description: Cypress standing in black water, and paths that are only paths this week.

biomes.name: The Sunward Steppe
biomes.description: Grass without end, broken by burial mounds and the smoke of somebody's camp.

biomes.name: The Glasslands
biomes.description: Dunes over fused sand, and a city that the sand mostly won.

biomes.name: The Sundered Isles
biomes.description: Rock, reef, and wreck. Everything here arrived by water or was left by it.

biomes.name: The Deeproads
biomes.description: Halls cut by hands and caverns cut by water, and no clean line between them.

biomes.name: Stone Town
biomes.description: Cut stone, tiled roofs, and streets that were planned by somebody.

biomes.name: Timber Town
biomes.description: Frame and thatch, a green, and lanes that were cow-paths first.

biomes.name: Delved Hold
biomes.description: Streets under a ceiling, lit by what the holds are willing to burn.

biomes.name: Sun Town
biomes.description: Whitewashed brick, shaded lanes, and every doorway facing away from the glare.

biomes.name: Wreck Town
biomes.description: Built out of what the sea returned, and standing on piles above it.

biomes.name: Barrow
biomes.description: Dry-stone chambers under a mound, built to be shut and not to be entered.

biomes.name: Delved Hall
biomes.description: Squared, dressed, and laid out by somebody with a plan and a workforce.

biomes.name: Cave
biomes.description: Cut by water over a very long time, and never intended for anyone.

biomes.name: Ruin
biomes.description: Roofless rooms with trees in them, and the plan still legible underfoot.

biomes.name: Burnt Deep
biomes.description: Worked ground that the mountain took back while it was still in use.

biomes.name: Drowned Works
biomes.description: Built dry, and standing in water now, and the water is winning.

biomes.name: Undercity
biomes.description: Drains, culverts, and the older streets they were cut through.

biomes.name: Ice Cave
biomes.description: Melt channels in a glacier, which move, and are therefore never twice the same shape.

areas.name: Aurenhal — Highgate
areas.description: The upper city: the Kingshold, the Grand Library, and the gate the Kingsroad actually arrives at.

areas.name: Aurenhal — Craftrow
areas.description: Every trade that needs a chimney, arranged along one long street by somebody who was thinking about fire.

areas.name: Aurenhal — Riverside
areas.description: Wharves, warehouses, and the river gate. The Weirwater does most of the city's carrying.

areas.name: Aurenhal — The Warrens
areas.description: Older than the wall that was built to contain it, and it has been leaking out of that wall ever since.

areas.name: Wraymill
areas.description: Six mills on one leat, a grain market, and the reason Aurenhal eats.

areas.name: Hollowdene
areas.description: A green, a well, a smithy, and eleven roofs. The road goes through rather than to it.

areas.name: Ashcott
areas.description: Sheep country. The village is mostly one lane and a very good hedge.

areas.name: Pennyford
areas.description: Named for what the ford used to cost. It is free now, and deeper.

areas.name: The Weirwater Crossing
areas.description: Where the Kingsroad meets the river on a bridge of nine arches, two of them younger than the rest.

areas.name: The Hedge Country
areas.description: Fields inside fields inside hedges laid before anybody's grandfather. Easy to walk and easy to lose a day in.

areas.name: The Kingsroad, South Reach
areas.description: Cut stone running dead straight to the southern horizon, with milestones counting down to places you have not been.

areas.name: The Oxbow Meadows
areas.description: The Weirwater changed its mind here a long time ago and left good grazing and bad drainage behind.

areas.name: Sarnport — Harbourside
areas.description: The harbour, the mole, and every trade that happens within a rope's throw of salt water.

areas.name: Sarnport — The Countinghouse
areas.description: Where the cargo becomes a number. Banks, brokers, insurers, and the harbour court.

areas.name: Sarnport — Saltcliff Rise
areas.description: Up the hill and out of the smell: the battery, the lighthouse road, and the houses of people who own ships rather than sail them.

areas.name: Cobbleway
areas.description: A market town a day inland of the harbour, and the last place a cart can be repaired before the downs.

areas.name: Gullmere
areas.description: Eleven boats, forty people, and a beach they haul up rather than a harbour they moor in.

areas.name: Thrift
areas.description: Named for the flower that grows on the cliff, not the habit, though both apply.

areas.name: The Chalk Downs
areas.description: Short turf over white rock, sheep, and a horse cut into the hillside by nobody anybody remembers.

areas.name: Wreckers' Strand
areas.description: Nine miles of shingle under a cliff, and everything the sea has given back for four hundred years still lying on it.

areas.name: Gannet Head
areas.description: The headland: four hundred feet of chalk, forty thousand birds, and a path along the top that is narrower than it was.

areas.name: Elderhollow
areas.description: Built in a clearing round an oak that the town is legally not allowed to touch.

areas.name: Rooksrest
areas.description: Charcoal burners, mostly, and the smoke never entirely leaves the clearing.

areas.name: Fenny Cross
areas.description: Where the forest road meets the coast road in a wet hollow, and everybody arriving is already in a bad mood.

areas.name: The Undereaves
areas.description: The edge of the forest, where the fields stop and do not start again for four days.

areas.name: The Moot Road
areas.description: The only road anybody keeps up, running straight to Elderhollow because the trees were persuaded to allow it.

areas.name: The Hollow Beeches
areas.description: A stand of beeches gone hollow with age, every one of them big enough to stand inside and several of them occupied.

areas.name: The Thornback Ride
areas.description: A cut through the forest going north, grown in to the width of one cart and closing.

areas.name: The Greenway
areas.description: Older than the Moot Road and straighter, and nobody cut it.

areas.name: The Witchwood
areas.description: Nine square miles the foresters will not work, and they will not be drawn on why.

areas.name: Karn Dolur — Gatehall
areas.description: The first hall inside the mountain: the gate, the muster floor, and everything the hold wants a stranger to see.

areas.name: Karn Dolur — The Deep Market
areas.description: A cavern the size of a town square with four galleries of shopfronts cut round the walls of it.

areas.name: Karn Dolur — The Forgetiers
areas.description: Six levels of furnace stacked down a shaft, and the shaft is the chimney.

areas.name: Highpass
areas.description: The last town on the road and the reason the road exists: a ward, a wall, and eleven hundred feet of altitude.

areas.name: Snowgate
areas.description: Nine houses, all of them dug half into the slope, and a bell to ring when the road is shut.

areas.name: The Cut
areas.description: A pass a hundred feet deep and forty wide, and somebody made it that way on purpose.

areas.name: The Ironstair
areas.description: Nine hundred steps up a cliff face to the gate of Karn Dolur, cut and railed and swept.

areas.name: The Cold Shoulder
areas.description: The north face, in shade from Emberfall to Greening, and the way to the ice.

areas.name: The Weirwater Head
areas.description: Where the river starts: a corrie, a lake, and a waterfall that goes into the ground rather than out of it.

areas.name: The Broken Road
areas.description: The old road up from the vale, taken out by a slip in the year of the great rains and never properly mended.

areas.name: Whalebone Landing
areas.description: Four hundred people, a harbour that freezes, and a meadhall built out of a jaw.

areas.name: Cairnhold
areas.description: Sixteen houses under one long roof, and eleven hundred cairns on the hill behind them.

areas.name: The Rimewatch Shore
areas.description: Where the ice meets the sea and neither gives ground. Bergs calve off it all summer with a noise like artillery.

areas.name: The White Reach
areas.description: Forty miles of level ice with nothing on it, in any direction, at all.

areas.name: The Bone Strand
areas.description: A beach of shingle and whale bone, where the whales have been coming ashore to die since before anyone watched.

areas.name: The Glass Ice
areas.description: Blue-black, swept bare by wind, and clear enough to see forty feet down into it.

areas.name: The Wind-Scoured Flats
areas.description: Where the wind has taken the snow away entirely and left the ice polished and the ground under it visible.

areas.name: The Last Cairn
areas.description: The furthest north anybody has built anything, and it is a heap of stones with a name.

areas.name: Barrowgate
areas.description: A market town with a keep, built on and partly out of a barrow that nobody has ever fully opened.

areas.name: Mirestead
areas.description: Peat cutters, on the only firm ground for two miles in any direction.

areas.name: Colder's Hearth
areas.description: Named for a man who kept a fire going here for forty years so people could find the way, and they still keep it going.

areas.name: Kestrel Edge
areas.description: The southern scarp: a gritstone edge two hundred feet high with the whole vale laid out below it.

areas.name: The Heatherlands
areas.description: Purple to the skyline in Winnow and brown the rest of the year, and no shelter anywhere in it.

areas.name: The Nine Sisters
areas.description: The highest ground on the moor, and nine stones standing on it in a ring sixty yards across.

areas.name: The Long Barrow
areas.description: Four hundred yards of raised ground running east and west, and it is all one grave.

areas.name: The Black Tarn
areas.description: A peat lake of no measured depth, with a shaft going down beside it that somebody cut.

areas.name: Cinderhold
areas.description: Built on its own slag heaps, walled in basalt, and hot enough that nobody lights a fire for warmth.

areas.name: Slagfoot
areas.description: At the foot of the vent fields, and the ground under the village is warm to the hand all year.

areas.name: The Ashfall
areas.description: Grey drift eight feet deep in the hollows, and it takes a footprint and keeps it for a season.

areas.name: The Obsidian Shelf
areas.description: Black glass in sheets a mile across, and every edge of it is an edge.

areas.name: The Smoking Road
areas.description: The only route across the reach that anybody keeps, marked by iron posts because nothing else survives being a marker.

areas.name: The Burnt March
areas.description: The western edge, where the ash thins and things start growing again, badly.

areas.name: The Vent Fields
areas.description: Four hundred acres of ground that breathes out, on schedules nobody has managed to write down.

areas.name: Firewatch Ridge
areas.description: The high ground on the northern side, with a chain of towers along it that were built to watch the mountain rather than the road.

areas.name: Stiltmarket
areas.description: Two thousand people on piles over open water, connected entirely by boardwalk and boat.

areas.name: Reedy Bottom
areas.description: Reed cutters on the western margin, where the swamp gives way to something you can nearly walk on.

areas.name: Drowned Bell
areas.description: Named for the one that is still down there and still, occasionally, audible.

areas.name: The Sunken Causeway
areas.description: A raised road under two feet of water for eleven miles, and it is the only hard bottom in the region.

areas.name: The Black Water
areas.description: Open water under cypress, of no honest depth, going in every direction and looking identical in all of them.

areas.name: The Cypress Maze
areas.description: Knees and trunks so thick you navigate by touch, and the channels between them close and open with the season.

areas.name: The Leech Channels
areas.description: Warm, slow, shallow, and thoroughly inhabited.

areas.name: The Hummocks
areas.description: Islands of firm ground, a few yards across, scattered across ten miles of water, and half of them have something on them.

areas.name: Ilkhet
areas.description: A town that is legally a camp, because moving it is still, in principle, an option.

areas.name: Three Wells
areas.description: Three, sunk in a line, and only two of them have ever gone dry at the same time.

areas.name: Tallgrass
areas.description: In the one place where the grass goes over head height, which is shelter of a kind and a nuisance of another.

areas.name: The Horse Road
areas.description: Not a road. A width of grass forty yards across that has been ridden flat for nine hundred years.

areas.name: The Kurgan Field
areas.description: Two hundred burial mounds in eleven rows, and the rows are aligned on something that is not the sun.

areas.name: The Long Grass
areas.description: Chest-high, unbroken, and it moves in a way that makes it very hard to tell what else is moving in it.

areas.name: The Dry River
areas.description: A bed a quarter of a mile wide with no water in it for eleven months and rather too much in the twelfth.

areas.name: The Windbreak
areas.description: A line of trees eleven miles long, planted, and there is no record of anybody planting it.

areas.name: The South Reach
areas.description: Where the grass thins, the ground pales, and the Glasslands start making themselves felt.

areas.name: Vashta Qal — The Oasis
areas.description: Palms, water, and eleven thousand people arranged in rings around the only spring for a hundred miles.

areas.name: Vashta Qal — The Glass Quarter
areas.description: Built on the lip of the crater, out of the crater, and the walls here are green and let light through.

areas.name: Saltrun
areas.description: Where the salt is cut, loaded, and argued about, on a flat that goes white to the horizon.

areas.name: Dry Cistern
areas.description: Named optimistically. It is dry nine years in ten and the tenth is why anybody stays.

areas.name: The Sunken Road
areas.description: A paved road under the dunes, showing in stretches where the wind has been kind, and going somewhere.

areas.name: The Shifting Dunes
areas.description: Two hundred feet high and moving south at about eleven yards a year, and everything under them is preserved.

areas.name: The Crater
areas.description: Four miles across, green glass from lip to lip, and something happened here.

areas.name: The Fulgurite Fields
areas.description: Where lightning has been fusing sand into branching glass tubes for longer than anybody has records, and the tubes stand up out of the ground like trees.

areas.name: The Bone Wells
areas.description: Eleven shafts sunk into the sand for water, all dry, all deep, and all of them full of something.

areas.name: Blackrigging
areas.description: A free port in the sense that nobody has successfully charged anything here, built out of about forty wrecks.

areas.name: Cormorant
areas.description: One rock, one jetty, and eleven families who have been here longer than Blackrigging has existed.

areas.name: Halfmast
areas.description: Built in and around a fort that the sea got into, and the fort is still the best building.

areas.name: The Narrows
areas.description: Eleven miles of shoal that moves between one season and the next, and the only way in.

areas.name: Wreck Reef
areas.description: The reason for the Narrows: a reef three miles long with about sixty ships on it in various stages of going.

areas.name: Gullstone
areas.description: A rock four hundred feet out of the water with nothing on it but birds and a stair.

areas.name: The Drowned Fort Shoal
areas.description: A fortress on a bank that the sea took, standing in twelve feet of water at low tide and forty at high.

areas.name: Tern Bank
areas.description: A shingle bank three miles long that is above water for nine months and a shoal for three.

areas.name: Lantern Deep
areas.description: Nine hundred people in a cavern, lit entirely by fungus and by what they can afford to burn.

areas.name: Mycelt
areas.description: A fungus farm with a village attached, and the village is very much the smaller half.

areas.name: The Long Hall
areas.description: Four miles of dressed corridor forty feet wide, running dead straight, with a ceiling nobody has surveyed.

areas.name: The Deep Market Road
areas.description: The one stretch that is genuinely a road, kept up by Lantern Deep and lit at intervals.

areas.name: The Fungus Gallery
areas.description: A cavern a mile across with a canopy of fungus forty feet up, and it is bright enough down here to read by.

areas.name: The Sunless River
areas.description: Sixty feet wide, no sound at all, and it has been going the same way for a very long time.

areas.name: The Black Bridge
areas.description: A single span over a chasm of no measured depth, with no parapet and no supports anybody can see.

areas.name: The Echo Halls
areas.description: Eleven chambers where a word comes back four times, each from a different direction.

areas.name: The Broken Stair
areas.description: A stair a hundred feet wide going up towards the Ember Reach, with about a third of it missing.

areas.name: The Weeping Vault
areas.description: Water comes through the roof here in ten thousand places and has been doing so long enough to build the floor up to meet it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Kingshold
pointsOfInterest.description: A castle that began as a river-fort and has been argued with by every monarch since.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Kingshold Undercroft
pointsOfInterest.description: Storerooms under the keep, and below those the older fort nobody has had a reason to survey.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grand Library
pointsOfInterest.description: Four floors of shelving and one very determined argument about who is allowed on the fourth.

pointsOfInterest.name: The High Temple
pointsOfInterest.description: The oldest roof in the city, and the only one the fire of 'eighty-one went round.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Mint
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the marks come from. Two doors, both watched.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Highgate Barracks
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the city watch sleeps, eats, and complains about the Warrens.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Goldsmiths' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: A guild that pretends to be about craft and is entirely about credit.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Scriptorium
pointsOfInterest.description: Copies made, letters written, contracts drawn, no questions logged.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Highgate Stables
pointsOfInterest.description: Where anybody with business at the Kingshold leaves their horse.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chancellor's Town House
pointsOfInterest.description: Three storeys, railings, and a door knocker shaped like something extinct.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wren's Lodging
pointsOfInterest.description: Rooms let by the month to clerks who wish they were closer to the Library.

pointsOfInterest.name: The King's Garden
pointsOfInterest.description: Walled, gravelled, and open to the public on days that keep changing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Six hearths under one roof, and a guild that decides whose iron gets which.

pointsOfInterest.name: Vench & Daughters, Armourers
pointsOfInterest.description: Plate, mail, and a very long wait unless you are somebody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bowyer's
pointsOfInterest.description: Staves seasoning in the rafters, some of them older than the bowyer.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sign of the Green Jar
pointsOfInterest.description: Drawers, jars, and a proprietor who wants to know exactly what for.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cooperage
pointsOfInterest.description: Barrels going out at one end and staves coming in at the other.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Tanyard
pointsOfInterest.description: Downwind of everything, by law, and still not far enough.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Glasshouse
pointsOfInterest.description: Southern sand, northern fuel, and a furnace that has not gone out in forty years.

pointsOfInterest.name: Craftrow Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Trestles up at dawn, down at dusk, and a fight about pitches in between.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Forge Arms
pointsOfInterest.description: Sooty, loud, and the best table in the city if you like being shouted at.

pointsOfInterest.name: Smiths' Row, Number Four
pointsOfInterest.description: One of nine identical houses, distinguished by the colour of the door.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ledd's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Workshop below, family above, and a stair between them that everyone is tired of.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Wharf
pointsOfInterest.description: Half a mile of stone quay, and never a free bollard when you want one.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Customs House
pointsOfInterest.description: Where a cargo becomes a number, and the number becomes an argument.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bonded Warehouse
pointsOfInterest.description: Locked, sealed, and rented by the cubic yard to people who like both.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chandlery
pointsOfInterest.description: Rope, tar, lamp oil, and every size of nail there is.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Boatyard
pointsOfInterest.description: River barges on the stocks, and one sea-going hull that will never fit under the bridge.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fish Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Loud from before dawn, over by nine, and washed down by ten.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ferryman's Rest
pointsOfInterest.description: Beds for boatmen, and a landlord who wakes you for the tide whether you asked or not.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Watergate Shrine
pointsOfInterest.description: A niche in the wall, a shelf of offerings, and a very old stain of candle-wax.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wharfinger's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Best window in the district and it looks directly at a warehouse wall.

pointsOfInterest.name: Netmenders' Row
pointsOfInterest.description: One long building divided eight ways, with the nets hung outside all of them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Undercity Grate
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the city's drains meet the river. It is not locked, which should tell you something.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Thieves' Market
pointsOfInterest.description: It has another name on the ward map. Nobody uses it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Three Balls, Anchor Lane
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything in the window was somebody's, once, and briefly.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Leaning Man
pointsOfInterest.description: The floor slopes, the stairs slope, and the landlord insists it is the customers.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bone Alley Shrine
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody keeps a light burning here and nobody will say who.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ratcatchers' Guild
pointsOfInterest.description: A real guild, with a charter, and rather more to do than the name suggests.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Gaol
pointsOfInterest.description: Emptied after the fire and never quite abandoned.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cellar Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: Behind a wine-shop that is not a wine-shop, a stair down into what the Warrens were built on top of.

pointsOfInterest.name: Kettle Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Six families, one pump, and a yard that is nobody's job.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Nunnery
pointsOfInterest.description: It has not been one for two hundred years and the name has outlived three rebuildings.

pointsOfInterest.name: Dogleg Lane
pointsOfInterest.description: The lane is why. The house is incidental.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Mill
pointsOfInterest.description: Four storeys of shaking timber over a wheel you can hear from the bridge.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grain Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Sacks, scales, and men arguing about moisture.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wraymill Smithy
pointsOfInterest.description: Millwork, mostly: gudgeons, bands, and the endless small iron of machines that shake.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wheel and Sheaf
pointsOfInterest.description: The only inn, and it knows it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Barrow's Provisions
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything a carter needs to get to Aurenhal and back.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wraymill Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Small, flint-built, and very cold in Deepdark.

pointsOfInterest.name: Coaching Stables
pointsOfInterest.description: Change here for Aurenhal, Cobbleway, or a long wait.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wraymill Brewery
pointsOfInterest.description: Uses the same leat as the mills, three hundred yards further down, which is a subject of correspondence.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Weaving Shed
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine looms, and the noise of nine looms.

pointsOfInterest.name: Millers' Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Built by the mill, rented from the mill, and dusted daily by the mill.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Reeve's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Stone below, timber above, and the only slate roof in the town.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hollowdene Green
pointsOfInterest.description: Grass, a whipping-post nobody uses, and the well. Everything in the village faces it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hollow Well
pointsOfInterest.description: Deeper than it needs to be, and cold all year.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hollowdene Smithy
pointsOfInterest.description: Shoes, hinges, and the occasional argument about a bill.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Village Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Salt, nails, thread, lamp oil, and gossip at no extra charge.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ploughshare
pointsOfInterest.description: Four tables, one fire, and beds upstairs if you do not mind the roof being close.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hollowdene Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, one bell, and a churchyard that has been filling slowly for six hundred years.

pointsOfInterest.name: Redding's Farm
pointsOfInterest.description: The biggest holding in the parish, which is not saying a great deal.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cottage on the Green
pointsOfInterest.description: Thatch down to the window-tops and a garden doing better than the house.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wold's
pointsOfInterest.description: Two rooms, a lean-to, and a dog with strong opinions.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dene Barrow
pointsOfInterest.description: A mound at the top of the sheep field with a stone doorway in the side, and the village has always told children to stay off it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ashcott Lane
pointsOfInterest.description: Not a green so much as a wide place in the lane, but it does the same job.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wool House
pointsOfInterest.description: Fleeces graded, weighed, and argued over from Reaping to Winnow.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ashcott Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Shears, mostly, and the mending of shears.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shepherd's Rest
pointsOfInterest.description: Two rooms to let and a landlady who counts the spoons.

pointsOfInterest.name: Long Hedge Farm
pointsOfInterest.description: Named for the hedge, which is genuinely remarkable and predates the farm.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sexton's Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Nearest house to the chapel, for reasons of convenience nobody enjoys.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Hedge
pointsOfInterest.description: Laid nine generations back and never once let through. It is a mile long and it goes where it wants.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ford
pointsOfInterest.description: Paved bottom, marker posts, and a depth board that has been optimistic since the sluice went in.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sluice House
pointsOfInterest.description: Winches, a chain, and a keeper's room with a very good view of the river doing whatever it likes.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ford Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Sells rope and dry stockings, in that order of profitability.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drowned Ox
pointsOfInterest.description: Named after an incident the landlord will describe at length.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Keeper's Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Close enough to the water to hear it change.

pointsOfInterest.name: Eel House
pointsOfInterest.description: Traps stacked to the eaves and a smell that never entirely leaves.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Nine Arches
pointsOfInterest.description: The bridge. Two of its arches were rebuilt after the flood and do not match, which locals will point out unprompted.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bridge Toll House
pointsOfInterest.description: Collects for the crown on one side and for the bridge fund on the other.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drowned Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Stands in the water at anything above summer level, and out of it in Highsun. Nobody has moved the altar.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Eel Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Half a dozen huts on the bank, occupied in season and left standing the rest of the year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Four Hedges
pointsOfInterest.description: Where four lanes meet at an angle none of them intended. There is a signpost and it has been turned.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hedge Wayshrine
pointsOfInterest.description: A stone hood over a stone shelf, with somebody's flowers in it, always.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Dovecote
pointsOfInterest.description: Round, roofless, and full of nesting boxes going back to stone.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Badger Hole
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody's terrier went in after something and came out the far side of the field, which is a longer set than a badger digs.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hundredth Milestone
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut with a number and a crown, and leaned on by everybody who gets this far.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Posting House
pointsOfInterest.description: Fresh horses, bad food, and a book you have to sign.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gibbet Oak
pointsOfInterest.description: Empty these forty years, and still nobody camps under it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Roadstone Quarry
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the Kingsroad came from. Worked out, flooded at the bottom, and not entirely empty.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Heronry
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty nests in a stand of dead alder, and the noise to match.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Withy Beds
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut every winter for baskets, and impassable every summer.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sunken Barge
pointsOfInterest.description: Went down loaded in somebody's grandfather's time. The ribs still show at low water.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Mole
pointsOfInterest.description: Half a mile of piled stone out into the bay, and the whole town is behind it in every sense.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Harbour Master's Office
pointsOfInterest.description: Decides who berths where and is not open to discussion about it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bond Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Four floors of other people's cargo, waiting on duty being paid.

pointsOfInterest.name: Rell's Chandlery
pointsOfInterest.description: Rope, canvas, tar, biscuit, and charts of varying honesty.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sail Loft
pointsOfInterest.description: One long room, one long floor, and canvas laid out the whole length of it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ropewalk
pointsOfInterest.description: A shed a quarter of a mile long and eight feet wide, because that is how rope is made.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Anchor Smith
pointsOfInterest.description: Chain, anchors, and fittings too big for anybody else's fire.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fish Quay
pointsOfInterest.description: Sold off the stones from four in the morning, and swept by eight.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Capstan
pointsOfInterest.description: Crews in, crews out, and a landlord who can tell which within a minute.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Seamen's Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Names on the wall in five columns and room left for a sixth.

pointsOfInterest.name: Netloft Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Living below, nets above, and a smell that has soaked into the beams.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Exchange
pointsOfInterest.description: A floor, a bell, and a great deal of shouting about cargoes nobody in the room has seen.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Harbour Court
pointsOfInterest.description: Where a collision, a salvage, or a mutiny becomes somebody's fault.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Insurers' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Men who make a living being right about how dangerous the sea is.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Countinghouse
pointsOfInterest.description: The building the district is named for. Three storeys of ledgers and one very good strongroom.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ottley's, Charts and Instruments
pointsOfInterest.description: Charts, compasses, glasses, and a proprietor who corrects you.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Goldsmith's
pointsOfInterest.description: Takes deposits, issues notes, and would rather you did not linger.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ledger
pointsOfInterest.description: A chophouse with rooms, where the food is incidental to the conversations.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Posting Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Coaches for Cobbleway and the Kingsvale, twice daily, weather allowing.

pointsOfInterest.name: Broker's Row, Number Nine
pointsOfInterest.description: Narrow, tall, and worth more than the street it stands in.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Clerks' Lodging
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven beds, one washstand, and a landlady with rules.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Saltcliff Light
pointsOfInterest.description: A hundred and ten feet of stone with a fire on top of it, and the keeper's stair going round the inside.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Saltcliff Battery
pointsOfInterest.description: Guns pointing at a sea nobody has come across in ninety years, kept up regardless.

pointsOfInterest.name: The High Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Up here for the view, which the priesthood insists is theological.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Rise Apothecary
pointsOfInterest.description: Serves the merchants' houses and charges them accordingly.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pilots' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Twenty men who know the bar, and will not write down how.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lantern
pointsOfInterest.description: Quiet, expensive, and with a window that looks straight down the harbour mouth.

pointsOfInterest.name: Vaunder House
pointsOfInterest.description: Four floors, a walled garden, and a family that owns eleven ships.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Keeper's Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Beside the light, and the light never lets it sleep properly.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cliff Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: Two hundred and forty steps from the Rise to the Quay, cut into the chalk and wet at the bottom.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chalk Workings
pointsOfInterest.description: Quarried out from under the Rise to build the town, and the town is now standing on the hole.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Market Cross
pointsOfInterest.description: Roofed, octagonal, and the whole reason there is a town here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Two Wheels
pointsOfInterest.description: Coaching inn, forty beds, and a yard that never entirely empties.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wheelwright's
pointsOfInterest.description: Tyres shrunk on hot in the yard, which the whole street comes out for.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cartwright's
pointsOfInterest.description: Bodies, shafts, and a stock of seasoned ash going back a decade.

pointsOfInterest.name: Fennick's
pointsOfInterest.description: Sells to farms, carters, and anybody heading for the downs.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Saddlery
pointsOfInterest.description: Harness, collars, and repairs while you wait if you are patient.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wayfarers' Church
pointsOfInterest.description: Big for the town, because the town used to be bigger.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Coach Stables
pointsOfInterest.description: Sixty stalls, and forty of them full on a market day.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bakehouse
pointsOfInterest.description: Bakes the town's bread and the town's pies in the same oven, in that order.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bailiff's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Sits at the top of the market place, looking down it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Tanyard Cottages
pointsOfInterest.description: Four under one roof, and the tanyard is no longer there, which everybody is glad about.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pound
pointsOfInterest.description: Stone walls, one gate, and any beast found straying goes in it until somebody pays.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Haul
pointsOfInterest.description: Shingle beach with eleven boats drawn up it and a capstan for each.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Beach Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Line, hooks, tar, and salt in the quantities a boat needs.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bass
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, one barrel, and a view of the weather coming.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Beach Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Fittings, hooks, and boat-nails, mostly.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sprat Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Three cottages gable-on to the sea, which is the only sensible way to build here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Net Loft
pointsOfInterest.description: Living underneath, mending above, and the smell of both.

pointsOfInterest.name: Thrift Green
pointsOfInterest.description: Cropped short by sheep and edged with the flower the place is named for.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cliff Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Last shop before the downs, and priced with that in mind.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pink
pointsOfInterest.description: Two rooms, and a landlord who will tell you about the flower.

pointsOfInterest.name: Thrift Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Flint and lime, and a bell that can be heard at Gullmere on a still night.

pointsOfInterest.name: Downs Farm
pointsOfInterest.description: Sheep, sheep, and a very good dog.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Coastguard
pointsOfInterest.description: Built to watch for smugglers and now lived in by their descendants.

pointsOfInterest.name: The White Horse
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut through the turf into the chalk, three hundred feet from nose to tail, and scoured every seventh year by everybody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dew Pond
pointsOfInterest.description: Clay-lined, on the top of a dry hill, and full. Nobody can entirely explain it and everybody uses it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shepherd's Hut
pointsOfInterest.description: On wheels, moved twice a year, and unlocked.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Flint Mines
pointsOfInterest.description: Shafts sunk into the chalk for flint before anybody here worked iron, and galleries running off every one of them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bone Beach
pointsOfInterest.description: Four hundred years of ribs and stem-posts standing out of the shingle at every angle.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lime Kiln
pointsOfInterest.description: Burnt the chalk to build Sarnport, and has been cold for sixty years.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wreckers' Hut
pointsOfInterest.description: Not the name they use. There is a good fire and a very good view of the bar.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Smugglers' Cave
pointsOfInterest.description: Goes in at the back of the beach and comes out somewhere up on the downs, which is the whole point of it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Stack
pointsOfInterest.description: Four hundred feet of chalk standing off the head, white with birds top to bottom.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cliff Path
pointsOfInterest.description: Two feet of turf between the fence and the drop, and the fence is advisory.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gannet Watchtower
pointsOfInterest.description: Built to see the fleet coming. It saw it, once, and has had nothing to do since.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sea Caves
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut by the sea into the foot of the head, and dry at the back for as far as anybody has gone.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Moot Oak
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine yards round at the base, hollow for the first twenty feet, and the town holds its moot inside it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Green Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Timber, charcoal, honey, hides, and a great deal of arguing about coppice rights.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Bough
pointsOfInterest.description: Beams out of the forest, floor out of the forest, and a fire that has never once gone out.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ring Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Axes, wedges, saw-teeth, and cart-iron for the timber wagons.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sawpit
pointsOfInterest.description: Two men, one saw, one very long day. Somebody is always in the pit and it is never the same somebody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Yew Shop
pointsOfInterest.description: Staves seasoning in the roof, some of them promised to people who have died waiting.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hask's
pointsOfInterest.description: Sells what the forest cannot provide, which is salt, iron, and news.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bee House
pointsOfInterest.description: Honey, wax, and mead, and the mead is the reason people come.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grove Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Roofed with shingles off the same oaks it was built between.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ox Lines
pointsOfInterest.description: Timber is hauled by oxen here, and there are forty of them.

pointsOfInterest.name: Warden's House
pointsOfInterest.description: The forest warden's, and it has a very large map on one wall.

pointsOfInterest.name: Coppice Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Five cottages built out of one very large tree, which is on record.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Burn
pointsOfInterest.description: Six charcoal clamps smouldering under turf, watched day and night for a fortnight at a time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Charcoal Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Sacks to the roof, and everything in the building is black.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Black Hand
pointsOfInterest.description: Named for what every customer's are. The ale is good and the upholstery is not.

pointsOfInterest.name: Burner's Hut
pointsOfInterest.description: A turf shelter that gets rebuilt wherever the clamp is that year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Lodge
pointsOfInterest.description: Built for a hunt that stopped coming, and lived in by four families since.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cross
pointsOfInterest.description: Forest road one way, coast road the other, and a foot of standing water in the middle of both.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wet Boot
pointsOfInterest.description: Honest about itself, which is the best thing anybody says about it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cross Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Dry stockings, lamp oil, and rope, in that order of turnover.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cross Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Mends wheels and axles for people who have just discovered the hollow.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Toll Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: There has been no toll for eighty years and the name has outlasted it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Duckboard House
pointsOfInterest.description: Reached by a plank, which says everything about the site.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Last Field
pointsOfInterest.description: Ploughed right up to the treeline, and the treeline has moved twice in the farmer's lifetime, both times the wrong way.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Woodward's Hut
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the forest warden sits when he wants to know who is going in.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Boundary Stones
pointsOfInterest.description: A line of them, half a mile apart, marking a boundary between two things that no longer exist.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Mile Oaks
pointsOfInterest.description: One planted at every mile, all on the same day, four hundred years ago, and all of them still standing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Moot Road Wayhouse
pointsOfInterest.description: A roof, a hearth, and a woodpile, kept by the town for anybody caught out after dark.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hollow Way
pointsOfInterest.description: The road before the road: sunk twenty feet below the forest floor and roofed over by four centuries of growth.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Beech King
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven yards round, hollow the whole way up, and you can stand in it and see sky.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hermit's Beech
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody has lived in this tree. The door is fitted properly.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Root Cellar
pointsOfInterest.description: Under the Beech King, and the roots are holding up a ceiling that is made of dressed stone.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Narrows
pointsOfInterest.description: The ride closes to eight feet here and the branches meet overhead, and it is dark at noon.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Burnt Lodge
pointsOfInterest.description: A hunting lodge that went up in somebody's grandfather's time, and the forest has taken three walls of four.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deadfall
pointsOfInterest.description: A tree came down and took a great deal of hillside with it, and under the hillside there was a doorway.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Avenue
pointsOfInterest.description: Two rows of oak a hundred feet apart running dead straight for six miles, and nobody planted them within record.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Green Bridge
pointsOfInterest.description: A single span of dressed stone over a stream you could step across, carved on both parapets, and older than the forest.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ride Barrow
pointsOfInterest.description: Sits directly on the Greenway, which means either the barrow came second or the road did.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ring
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine trees in a circle sixty feet across, all the same age, all the same species, and nothing at all growing inside them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Leaning Tower
pointsOfInterest.description: Four storeys of elf-work with a beech growing through it, holding it up and pulling it apart at once.

pointsOfInterest.name: Under the Ring
pointsOfInterest.description: There is a stair inside the Ring, going down, and the ninth tree has grown over the top of it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Still Pool
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty feet across, black, and no wind has ever moved it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hold Gate
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty tons of stone on a counterweight, and two of the hold's own on either side of it at all hours.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Muster Floor
pointsOfInterest.description: Six hundred feet of flagged hall, kept empty, which is itself the statement.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wardens' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Who comes in, who goes out, and who is answerable for both.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lamp Works
pointsOfInterest.description: Every lamp in the hold is filled from here and there are eleven thousand of them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gate Outfitters
pointsOfInterest.description: Lamps, rope, cleats, and cold-weather gear for people going out.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Counterweight
pointsOfInterest.description: First inn inside the gate, and it charges for the privilege.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shrine of the First Cut
pointsOfInterest.description: Marks the spot where the hold was begun, which is nine hundred feet from where it now starts.

pointsOfInterest.name: Gatewarden's Lodging
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut into the wall beside the gate, so the warden is never more than a minute from it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Visitors' Cells
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the hold puts people it has not decided about yet.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ledger Stone
pointsOfInterest.description: Every gate-fee since the hold was cut, in columns, and the columns go round three walls.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Market Floor
pointsOfInterest.description: A cavern the size of a town square, four galleries of shopfronts cut round it, and a roof you cannot see.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Stone Merchant
pointsOfInterest.description: Sells rock, by weight, by grade, and by argument.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Oil Gallery
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven grades of lamp oil and a proprietor who can smell the difference.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Provisioner
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything that keeps, in a place where nothing grows.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fungus Rows
pointsOfInterest.description: Grown three levels down and sold up here, and about a third of it is medicine.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hall of Measures
pointsOfInterest.description: Where a weight becomes a legal weight, and where the standards themselves are kept.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lamplit
pointsOfInterest.description: Four hundred years old, entirely underground, and there is a waiting list for the corner table.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Shrine
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut so that a single lamp lights the whole chamber, which took somebody a lifetime to work out.

pointsOfInterest.name: Fourth Gallery, Thirteen
pointsOfInterest.description: A shop below and a family above, cut out of one block.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Weighers' Rooms
pointsOfInterest.description: Lodging for the hall's clerks, and a view down onto the floor.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Six levels of furnace stacked down a shaft that serves as the chimney for all of them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Platers' Tier
pointsOfInterest.description: Armour, and a waiting list measured in seasons.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Edge Tier
pointsOfInterest.description: Blades only, and they will not discuss anything else.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wire Drawers
pointsOfInterest.description: Draw-plates in fifty sizes and a smell of hot tallow.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ore Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Graded, weighed, and stacked by seam of origin.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bellows Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: The waterwheel that drives every bellows in the tier, fed from a shaft nobody is allowed to look down.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Slack Tub
pointsOfInterest.description: Loud, hot, and closed for one hour a day to be swept.

pointsOfInterest.name: Smiths' Cells
pointsOfInterest.description: Sixty rooms off one corridor, and the corridor is warm all year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Door
pointsOfInterest.description: The way to the levels the hold gave up: sealed, marked, and inspected monthly.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Seams
pointsOfInterest.description: Worked out four hundred years ago and left open, because a hold does not fill in what it might want back.

pointsOfInterest.name: Highpass Ward
pointsOfInterest.description: A wall across the valley with a gate in it, and a garrison who spend most of the year shovelling.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ward Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Three days a week, and only in the four months anybody can get here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Last House
pointsOfInterest.description: Genuinely the last one, in the direction that matters.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ward Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Cleats, crampons, shovel-blades, and cart-iron.

pointsOfInterest.name: Skarn Outfitters
pointsOfInterest.description: Ropes, lamps, furs, and honest advice about the pass.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ward Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Small, thick-walled, and warm, which is the whole of its appeal.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Mule Lines
pointsOfInterest.description: Nothing above Highpass goes by cart. Ninety mules live here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ward Bakehouse
pointsOfInterest.description: Bakes for the garrison first and the town second, and says so.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Captain's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Stone, slate, and shutters two inches thick.

pointsOfInterest.name: Shovellers' Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Built for the men who keep the road open, which is most of the town.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ward Cellars
pointsOfInterest.description: The wall has more below it than above, and some of the below is older than the wall.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Snowgate Bell
pointsOfInterest.description: Rung when the road shuts. It is heard at Highpass and at Karn Dolur both.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gate Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Sells fuel, fat, and rope, and buys nothing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drift
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, dug into the slope, and warmer than anywhere in Highpass.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Snowgate Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Sharpens ice-tools and mends the bell frame, which needs it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep House
pointsOfInterest.description: Dug in eleven feet, and it does not need a fire until Rimewatch.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Watch Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody sits here and looks north, all winter, in shifts.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cut
pointsOfInterest.description: A hundred feet deep, forty wide, dead straight, and the tool marks are still on the walls.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Toll Fort
pointsOfInterest.description: Built across the Cut to charge for it, and slighted by somebody who objected.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cut Galleries
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the stone from the Cut went, and the galleries go a great deal further than the stone would account for.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ironstair
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine hundred steps up a cliff face, cut, railed, and swept daily by somebody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Halfway House
pointsOfInterest.description: A cut chamber at step four hundred and fifty with a bench and a brazier.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fallen Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: The first stair, which came off the cliff in one piece four hundred years ago and is lying at the bottom.

pointsOfInterest.name: The North Face
pointsOfInterest.description: In shade from Emberfall to Greening, and the snow on it is older than anybody using the road.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ice Road
pointsOfInterest.description: A snow bridge over a gap of unknown depth. It is there in winter. It is not there in summer.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wind Cave
pointsOfInterest.description: Blows out at dawn and in at dusk, hard enough to lean on, which means it goes a very long way.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Corrie Lake
pointsOfInterest.description: Black, round, three hundred feet deep at the middle, and the start of the Weirwater.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Swallet
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the whole outflow goes into the ground rather than down the valley, and comes out somewhere nobody has proved.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sink
pointsOfInterest.description: Follows the water in. It has been followed for two miles and somebody did not come back from the third.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Slip
pointsOfInterest.description: Half a mile of the old road, and the hillside it was on, at the bottom of the valley.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Broken Road Wayhouse
pointsOfInterest.description: Built for the traffic the road used to carry, and running at about a fifth of that.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Broken Bridge
pointsOfInterest.description: Three arches standing and two not, and the river going through the gap perfectly happily.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Jawbone
pointsOfInterest.description: A meadhall roofed on the jaw of something that came ashore in somebody's great-grandmother's time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Landing
pointsOfInterest.description: Not a harbour. A shelving beach, a capstan, and eight months a year of ice.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Oil Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Whale oil in butts, stacked four high, and the whole building is worth more than the town.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Flensing Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Where a whale becomes oil, bone, and a smell you will not forget.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Landing Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Harpoon irons, flensing knives, and everything else sharp.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Landing Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Furs, fat, iron, and rope, and no fresh anything at any price.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bone Carver
pointsOfInterest.description: Scrimshaw, buttons, combs, and one very large chess set.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ice Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Thick-walled, low-doored, and warmer than the meadhall.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Blubber
pointsOfInterest.description: Nobody remembers its real name. Everybody knows what it smells of.

pointsOfInterest.name: Harpooner's Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Turf over timber over turf, and warm as a burrow.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Factor's House
pointsOfInterest.description: The only two-storey building. It buys the oil and sells the everything.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cairn Field
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven hundred of them on the hill behind the village, and somebody knows what every one is for.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Roof
pointsOfInterest.description: Sixteen households under one roof, because sixteen roofs would be sixteen roofs to keep clear.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hold Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Held in common, drawn against by the winter, and audited furiously.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cairn Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: One fire, run for two hours a day, because fuel comes by sled.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Keeper's Shrine
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the cairn-keepers are trained, which takes eleven years.

pointsOfInterest.name: Under the First Cairn
pointsOfInterest.description: The oldest one, and the only one anybody has ever opened, and they stopped.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Calving Face
pointsOfInterest.description: Two hundred feet of ice cliff going into the sea, and it lets go twice a day all summer with a noise like a siege.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Rimewatch Hut
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody sits here and counts the bergs going out, for reasons that made sense to whoever started it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Blue Caves
pointsOfInterest.description: Melt channels in the face, open at the bottom of the cliff, and they go somewhere different every year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Middle of the Reach
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty miles of level ice, and this is the point equidistant from every edge of it, and it is marked.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Depot
pointsOfInterest.description: A sledge-load of fuel and food buried under a flag, restocked by whoever passes and used by whoever needs it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Frozen Ship
pointsOfInterest.description: Thirty miles from open water, upright, with her masts still standing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Boneyard
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the whales have come ashore to die since before there was anybody to watch, and the shingle is more bone than stone.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Strand Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Used in the two months the ice lets anybody work here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ribcage
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody has built into the ribs of the largest of them, and then gone on building downward.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Clear
pointsOfInterest.description: Swept bare by wind and transparent for forty feet down, and there are things at thirty.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Moulin
pointsOfInterest.description: A shaft the meltwater has drilled straight down through the glacier, and in winter it is dry.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bearing Marker
pointsOfInterest.description: A pole in the ice with four arms, and three of them point at nothing you can see.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pavement
pointsOfInterest.description: Polished ice over bare rock, and you can see the rock, and it has been quarried.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Stone Rows
pointsOfInterest.description: Rows of set stones under the ice, visible and unreachable, going on for half a mile.

pointsOfInterest.name: Under the Pavement
