pointsOfInterest.description: The wind has taken enough ice off to open a way into whatever was quarried here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Last Cairn
pointsOfInterest.description: A heap of stones, chest high, and the furthest north anybody has built anything.

pointsOfInterest.name: The North Shelter
pointsOfInterest.description: Three walls, a roof, and a door that opens inward because of the drifts.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hollow
pointsOfInterest.description: The cairn is on top of something and the something has a way in.

pointsOfInterest.name: Barrowgate Keep
pointsOfInterest.description: Built on the barrow, out of the barrow, and by people who were explicitly told not to.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Moot Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the moor's business is done: grazing rights, peat rights, and the one subject nobody raises.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Barrow Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Wool, peat, and mutton, on the flat ground beside the mound rather than on it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Standing Stone
pointsOfInterest.description: There is one, in the yard, and the inn was built around rather than moving it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gate Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Peat spades, turf irons, and the ironwork for eleven miles of wall.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hasp's
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything the moor cannot grow, which is nearly everything.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wool Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Graded and sold twice a year and the town lives off both days.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Church on the Mound
pointsOfInterest.description: Built on the east end of the barrow, deliberately, and the foundations went into something.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Moor Stables
pointsOfInterest.description: Ponies, not horses. Anything taller is no use up here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Constable's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Beside the keep, and the constable does not sleep in the keep.

pointsOfInterest.name: Peatman's Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Six cottages, each with a peat stack against the gable taller than the door.

pointsOfInterest.name: Under the Keep
pointsOfInterest.description: The keep's cellars go into the barrow, which the builders swore they would not do.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cuttings
pointsOfInterest.description: Faces of black peat eight feet high, cut in steps, and drying stacks between them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Turf
pointsOfInterest.description: Burns peat, obviously, and the smell is in everything including the beer.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cutters' Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Spades, boots, rope, and dry socks.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Mire Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Peat spades and turf irons, and it makes nothing else at all.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dry House
pointsOfInterest.description: On the only rock in the village, and every other house envies it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Duckboard Cottages
pointsOfInterest.description: Reached by planks, and the planks are municipal property.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Cutting
pointsOfInterest.description: They cut down eleven feet here and found a floor, and stopped cutting.

pointsOfInterest.name: Colder's Fire
pointsOfInterest.description: Kept burning for forty years by one man so that people could find the way, and kept burning since by everybody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Beacon
pointsOfInterest.description: Exists to take in whoever the fire brought.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hearth Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Fuel, mostly. Fuel is the local currency and the local anxiety.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Small Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, and the fire is visible through its one window.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Keeper's Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Whoever lives here tends the fire. It is not a job you apply for.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wayfarers' Rest
pointsOfInterest.description: Beds for people the moor nearly kept, and there are several every winter.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Edge
pointsOfInterest.description: Two hundred feet of gritstone with the whole Kingsvale laid out below it, and kestrels hanging along the whole length.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shooting House
pointsOfInterest.description: Built for a sport that stopped, and used since by shepherds and whoever else.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grit Caves
pointsOfInterest.description: Where blocks have come away from the edge and left slots behind them, and one of the slots does not end.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Moor Crossing
pointsOfInterest.description: A line of marker stones a hundred paces apart, and in poor visibility it is the only thing standing between you and a very long walk.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Heather Bothy
pointsOfInterest.description: Unlocked, unstaffed, stocked, and it has saved more lives than the keep has.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Burnt Farm
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody tried to farm up here, once, and the moor was extremely clear about it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Nine Sisters
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine stones in a ring sixty yards across, on the highest ground for twenty miles, and none of them is local rock.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fallen Sister
pointsOfInterest.description: The tenth, lying down, with writing on the underside that somebody has propped it up to read.

pointsOfInterest.name: Beneath the Sisters
pointsOfInterest.description: A stair between the two eastern stones, going down, cut into the gritstone and worn in the middle.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Barrow
pointsOfInterest.description: Four hundred yards of raised ground running east and west, and it is all one grave.

pointsOfInterest.name: The East End
pointsOfInterest.description: The only way in that anybody has found, at the sunrise end, behind a slab that has been moved before.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Diggers' Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody excavated here for two seasons, wrote nothing down that survives, and left in a hurry.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Black Tarn
pointsOfInterest.description: Peat-black, forty yards across, and every attempt to sound it has run out of line.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Tarn Shaft
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut square, beside the water, with rungs in the wall and the first thirty feet of them rusted through.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sunken Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Shows above the water in a dry Highsun and not otherwise, and it is the wrong shape for a chapel.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Slag Cathedral
pointsOfInterest.description: Cast rather than built: they poured it, over eleven years, and it has no joints anywhere.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Black Wall
pointsOfInterest.description: Basalt, forty feet, and it is not there to keep people out.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Glass Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Obsidian by the sheet, by the flake, and by the finished edge.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Foundry
pointsOfInterest.description: Uses the ground for half its heat, which is why the town is here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Edge Shop
pointsOfInterest.description: Obsidian blades: sharper than steel, and they last about nine minutes.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ore Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Iron out of the reach, graded and stacked and waiting for a cart brave enough.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Reach Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Water, mostly. Water is the expensive thing here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ash Apothecary
pointsOfInterest.description: Burns, lungs, and the specific things the reach does to people.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cold Room
pointsOfInterest.description: Dug down rather than built up, and it is the only cool building in the town, and it is not cool.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Vent Readers' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty people who can tell you what the ground will do tomorrow, and are right about four days in five.

pointsOfInterest.name: Basalt Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Walls three feet thick, one window, and it stays at the same temperature all year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Founder's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Cast, like the cathedral, by somebody proving a point.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Slag Door
pointsOfInterest.description: In the floor of the cathedral, cast shut in one piece, and the cathedral was built to have it there.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Warm Ground
pointsOfInterest.description: You can lie on it in Deepdark and be comfortable, and people do, and occasionally it goes wrong.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Kettle
pointsOfInterest.description: Boils its water by standing the pot on the floor.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Foot Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Water, boots, and the good kind of gloves.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ground Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Has no fire of its own. Does not need one.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Reader's Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Whoever reads the vents lives here, at the front, closest to them.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sulphur Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Three cottages built out of the same cooled flow they stand on.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lava Tube
pointsOfInterest.description: A flow drained out from under its own crust and left a tunnel twenty feet across going into the mountain.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drifts
pointsOfInterest.description: Eight feet deep in the hollows, and it takes a footprint and keeps it until the next fall.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Buried Village
pointsOfInterest.description: Roofs showing above the ash in a line, and everything below the roofs is exactly as it was left.

pointsOfInterest.name: Under the Roofs
pointsOfInterest.description: You go in through a chimney and down into a street.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sheet
pointsOfInterest.description: A mile of black glass, flat, and it reflects the sky in a way that stops being pleasant after a while.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cutters' Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the glass is quarried, by people who work in leather from neck to ankle in that heat.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Broken Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: A stair going down through the glass, cut before the glass was there, which is not a thing that can be true.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Iron Posts
pointsOfInterest.description: A hundred paces apart, all the way across, because nothing else survives being a marker here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Road Station
pointsOfInterest.description: Stone, thick, with a water cistern under it and a bell on top.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lost Cart
pointsOfInterest.description: Off the line of posts by forty yards, and it has been there since before the posts.

pointsOfInterest.name: The New Treeline
pointsOfInterest.description: Where things start growing again, badly, and the line has moved east twice in living memory.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ash Farm
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody is farming the ash, which is extraordinarily fertile once it has had thirty years.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Workings
pointsOfInterest.description: Iron was got here before the reach caught fire, and the workings were left in the middle of a shift.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chain
pointsOfInterest.description: Iron posts and a chain, and past the chain the ground breathes on its own schedule.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Vent
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty feet across, and it goes off about every nine hours, and you can set a watch by it if you are willing to stand there.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Throat
pointsOfInterest.description: Down the side of the Great Vent, on ledges, between eruptions.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Firewatch Towers
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine of them along the ridge, built to watch the mountain rather than the road, and four are still manned.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fallen Tower
pointsOfInterest.description: The fifth. It went over in the year of the ashfall and the garrison went with it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Signal Deep
pointsOfInterest.description: Under the seventh tower there is a shaft, and it was there before the tower, and the tower was put on top of it deliberately.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Boardwalk
pointsOfInterest.description: An inn, a market, and four hundred feet of covered walk, all of it one building on nine hundred piles.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Water Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Sold boat to boat, in a basin, and nobody involved is standing on anything.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pile Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Drives the piles the town stands on, and the town needs about four hundred a year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Punt Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Flat-bottomed, shallow-draught, and every one of them made to the same pattern for six hundred years.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Floating Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: On a barge, moored, because the town will not have a fire on piles.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dry Store
pointsOfInterest.description: The clue is the name and the name is the entire business model.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fever House
pointsOfInterest.description: Bark, quinine, and a brisk trade in things for the fever.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Reed Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut, bundled, dried, and shipped out as the region's one export.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Water Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: On its own piles, apart from the rest, reached by one walk.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pole
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the punt-men drink, which is to say where the news is.

pointsOfInterest.name: Third Walk, Eleven
pointsOfInterest.description: Two rooms over water, and the floor moves when the wind gets up.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pilot's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Whoever takes boats out through the shoals lives here and is wealthy.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Reed Beds
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut every winter, in blocks, on a nine-year rotation that everybody in the village can recite.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bundle
pointsOfInterest.description: Thatched, obviously, and rethatched every third year out of principle.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cutters' Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Hooks, whetstones, waders, and rope.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Thatcher's
pointsOfInterest.description: Trains four apprentices at a time and has a waiting list of eleven years.

pointsOfInterest.name: Bottom Farm
pointsOfInterest.description: The only ploughed land in the region and it is under water two years in five.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wader's Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Boots by the door, eleven pairs, all of them somebody's.

pointsOfInterest.name: The New Bell Tower
pointsOfInterest.description: Built directly over the old one, which is under it, and under water.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ringers
pointsOfInterest.description: Six ringers, one inn, and they will tell you about the bell.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bell Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything, in small quantities, at swamp prices.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chapel Above
pointsOfInterest.description: The second one on this site. The first is beneath it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sexton's
pointsOfInterest.description: Keeps the keys to the belfry hatch and does not lend them.

pointsOfInterest.name: Pile Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Rebuilt four times as the water came up, each time nine inches higher.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Church
pointsOfInterest.description: Down the hatch, past the old bell, into a nave that has been under water for two hundred years and is not full.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Causeway
pointsOfInterest.description: A raised road under two feet of water for eleven miles, and the only hard bottom in the region.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Marker House
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody lives on the causeway and resets the marker poles after every flood, which is often.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Toll House
pointsOfInterest.description: Stood on the causeway when the causeway was dry, and is now standing in it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ferry Crossing
pointsOfInterest.description: A punt, a pole, and a man who has done this for thirty-one years and will not be hurried.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dead Stand
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty acres of cypress that died standing, all in the same year, and nobody knows which year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sunken Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: A roof-ridge showing above the water, and below it a hall, and below the hall a floor that is dry.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Knees
pointsOfInterest.description: Cypress roots up out of the water in thousands, waist-high, and you navigate this by touch.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hunter's Stand
pointsOfInterest.description: A platform in a tree with a ladder, and somebody keeps the ladder in repair.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cypress Mound
pointsOfInterest.description: A rise in the middle of the maze that is not a natural rise, with a way into the side of it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Warm Channels
pointsOfInterest.description: Blood-warm, slow, shallow, and thoroughly inhabited by things that appreciate all three.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Leech Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: They are farmed here and sold to every apothecary in the south, which is a living.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drowned Mill
pointsOfInterest.description: There was a fall of water here once, which means the land was different, which is worth thinking about.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hummocks
pointsOfInterest.description: Islands of firm ground a few yards across, scattered over ten miles, and about half of them have something on them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hermit's Hummock
pointsOfInterest.description: One hut, one garden, one grave, and all three well kept by somebody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Hummock
pointsOfInterest.description: The largest of them, and the only one made of stone rather than silt, and there is a way down through it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Khan's Yurt
pointsOfInterest.description: Sixty feet across, felt over a lattice, and it comes down in two hours if it has to.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Horse Fair
pointsOfInterest.description: Four times a year, and the town exists to hold it and to argue about it for the rest of the time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Horse Lines
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven hundred animals, picketed in rows, and every one of them known by somebody.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Farriers' Ring
pointsOfInterest.description: Six fires in a circle, all working, and the circle is the point.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Saddlery
pointsOfInterest.description: Trees, panels, and the particular geometry of a saddle that will be lived in for eleven hours a day.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Horn Bowyer
pointsOfInterest.description: Horn, sinew, and glue, and the finished bow takes four years.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Trade Yurt
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything from the north, at four times what it costs in the north.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Felt Makers
pointsOfInterest.description: Roofs, walls, boots, and blankets, all from the same process and all of it smells the same.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Stirrup
pointsOfInterest.description: Timber, which is a statement, and it is the only timber building for ninety miles.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sky Shrine
pointsOfInterest.description: Open to the top, deliberately, and it rains in and that is considered correct.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Standing Yurts
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine that have not been moved in three generations, which is a quiet scandal.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Winter Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Dug in and turfed over, and used four months in twelve.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Three Wells
pointsOfInterest.description: Sunk in a line a hundred paces apart, and only two of them have ever gone dry in the same year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bucket
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, and the well-head is inside it, which is either clever or unhygienic.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Well Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Rope, leather buckets, and a great deal of rope.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Well Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Chain, windlass gear, and horseshoes.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Waterman's
pointsOfInterest.description: Whoever keeps the wells lives between the first and the second.

pointsOfInterest.name: Rope Cottage
pointsOfInterest.description: Makes rope, sells rope, and has rope in every room.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dry Well
pointsOfInterest.description: The fourth, which nobody counts, and which went dry two hundred years ago and has a doorway at the bottom.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Tall Stand
pointsOfInterest.description: Grass over head height for eleven acres, and you can lose a horse in it and frequently do.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Scythe
pointsOfInterest.description: Named for the only tool that has ever made any difference here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cut Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Blades, whetstones, and hay forks.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grass Shrine
pointsOfInterest.description: Mown, in a circle, by hand, every week, by whoever is free.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Mown Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Keeps a bare ring round the house because of what the grass does in a dry Reaping.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hayward's
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut, stacked, and sold to Ilkhet for the winter lines.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Horse Road
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty yards of grass ridden flat over nine hundred years, and it is not a road and everybody calls it one.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Relay Post
pointsOfInterest.description: Fresh horses every thirty miles, which is how news crosses the steppe in three days.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Stone Horse
pointsOfInterest.description: Carved, life-size, lying on its side where it fell, and there is no stone within forty miles.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Skull Line
pointsOfInterest.description: Horse skulls on poles, a hundred paces apart, and no rider will cross it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Kurgans
pointsOfInterest.description: Two hundred mounds in eleven rows, aligned on something, and the something is not the sun.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Kurgan
pointsOfInterest.description: The largest, at the head of the middle row, and it is the only one with a way in.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grass Sea
pointsOfInterest.description: Chest-high and unbroken to the horizon, moving in a way that makes it very hard to tell what else is moving in it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Watch Mound
pointsOfInterest.description: Twelve feet of raised earth, and it is the only place in nine miles you can see out of the grass.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lost Wagons
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven of them in a defensive ring, in grass, four days from any route.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Dry Bed
pointsOfInterest.description: A quarter of a mile wide, with nothing in it for eleven months and a great deal in it for the twelfth.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ford Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Used by everybody crossing, and struck at the first sign of weather upstream.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cut Bank
pointsOfInterest.description: The flood took a bite out of the bank and opened a stair that had been in it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Windbreak
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven miles of trees in a single line, planted, and no record anywhere of anybody planting them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shade Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: The only shade on the steppe, and consequently the most contested ground in the region.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Planter's Stone
pointsOfInterest.description: At the western end, cut with a great many names and one date.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pale Ground
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the grass thins and the ground goes white, and the Glasslands start making themselves felt.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Last Water
pointsOfInterest.description: A spring, a trough, and a very firm local convention about who drinks in what order.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sand Shaft
pointsOfInterest.description: Sand pours into it continuously and it never fills, which has been true for as long as anybody has watched.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Spring
pointsOfInterest.description: The only water for a hundred miles, and eleven thousand people are arranged in rings around it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sunken Bath
pointsOfInterest.description: Built when the water was forty feet higher, and the top three storeys of it are now the bottom three.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shade Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Under awnings, all of it, and the awnings are municipal and somebody's whole department.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Water Wardens
pointsOfInterest.description: Decide who drinks, how much, and in what order, and are the single most powerful body in the south.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Date Halls
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven varieties, graded, and the grading is a profession.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Caravan Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Water skins, salt, rope, and shade cloth.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Potters' Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Water jars, in four sizes, and the four sizes are legally defined.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Oasis Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Charcoal comes eleven days by camel, so nothing is forged here that could be forged elsewhere.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Temple of the Spring
pointsOfInterest.description: Built over the spring head, and the priesthood and the wardens have been the same people for four hundred years.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Palm
pointsOfInterest.description: Courtyard, fountain, and rooms that face inward away from the sun.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Camel Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Four hundred of them, and the smell is a permanent feature of the eastern city.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Second Ring
pointsOfInterest.description: Whitewashed, thick-walled, and it faces away from the street on every side.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Warden's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Closest of any private house to the spring, which is the entire message.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Crater Lip
pointsOfInterest.description: The quarter is built on it, out of it, and the walls let light through.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Glass Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Green glass by the block and by the finished piece, and the finished pieces go north for a great deal of money.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cutters' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Crater glass is cut cold, never worked hot, for reasons nobody here will discuss with a stranger.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lens Maker
pointsOfInterest.description: Glasses, burning lenses, and one instrument in the window that nobody will price.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Glass Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Packed in sand, crated, and shipped north eleven times a year.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Green Room
pointsOfInterest.description: The walls are crater glass and the light inside it is a colour you will not find anywhere else.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shrine on the Lip
pointsOfInterest.description: Faces the crater rather than the city, which was a decision.

pointsOfInterest.name: Cutters' Terrace
pointsOfInterest.description: Green-walled, and the residents claim it is cooler and it is not.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Consulate
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody's embassy, once, to a city that has since stopped existing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Crater Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut down the inside of the lip, in glass, and it goes below the floor of the crater.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salt Pans
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut in squares, flooded, evaporated, and cut again, over about eleven square miles.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salt Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Weighed, graded, and argued about, and the arguing is where the money is.

pointsOfInterest.name: The White House
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything in Saltrun is white. This one is whiter.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Run Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Shovels, rakes, barrows, and eye protection.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salt Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything corrodes here in a season, so the forge never stops.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salt Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Blocks stacked in a building made of blocks.

pointsOfInterest.name: The White Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Built of salt block, which means it is dissolving, slowly, and is rebuilt every generation.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Camel Lines
pointsOfInterest.description: Salt goes out by camel and there is no other way it goes.

pointsOfInterest.name: Pan Cottages
pointsOfInterest.description: Six, in a row, all with white-rimed boots outside.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Weigher's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Has the only accurate scales in the region and is guarded accordingly.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Pan
pointsOfInterest.description: They cut down through the salt looking for better grade and came out the bottom of it into a room.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cistern
pointsOfInterest.description: Roman in its ambition and empty nine years in ten, and the tenth is why anybody stays.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drop
pointsOfInterest.description: Named for what everyone here is waiting for.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cistern Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Water at a price that would be criminal anywhere else.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Keeper's
pointsOfInterest.description: Whoever measures the cistern lives beside it and does so daily.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Waiting Houses
pointsOfInterest.description: Four, empty most years, occupied entirely in the wet one.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Feeder
pointsOfInterest.description: The channel that fills the cistern, walked upstream, in the nine years when it is dry enough to walk.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Paving
pointsOfInterest.description: A dressed road under the dunes, showing in stretches where the wind has been kind, and going somewhere.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Caravanserai
pointsOfInterest.description: Four walls, one gate, a well, and it has been here since the road was above ground.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Milepost Vault
pointsOfInterest.description: One of the mileposts is hollow and there is a stair in it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Crest
pointsOfInterest.description: Two hundred feet high and moving south at about eleven yards a year, and everything under it is preserved.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Uncovered Town
pointsOfInterest.description: The dune moved off it eleven years ago and will move back over it in about thirty.

pointsOfInterest.name: Under the Uncovered Town
pointsOfInterest.description: The cellars are intact because sand is an excellent roof.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Thin Glass
pointsOfInterest.description: The glass gets thin about a mile in, and the thin part is over something.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Centre
pointsOfInterest.description: Four miles from any lip, and the glass here is clear rather than green, and you can see down.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Centre Shaft
pointsOfInterest.description: Straight down from the middle, glass-walled, and whatever made the crater went this way.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Glass Grove
pointsOfInterest.description: Branching tubes of fused sand standing eleven feet out of the ground, in thousands, where lightning has been striking the same field for a very long time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Collectors' Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Fulgurite is worth money and getting it out whole is a skill.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Root
pointsOfInterest.description: One tube goes down rather than up, and it is wide enough, and somebody has widened it further.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bone Wells
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven shafts sunk for water, all dry, all deep, and all of them full of something.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Diggers' Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody sank these. Somebody else has been coming back to look at what is in them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ninth Well
pointsOfInterest.description: The only one with rungs, and they go down further than the shaft was ever dug.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Weatherly
pointsOfInterest.description: A merchantman that came ashore stern-first in 'eighty-one and has been an inn ever since without anybody moving her.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Free Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Nobody has ever successfully charged a fee here, and several people have tried, and there is a list.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hulks
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven ships moored in a row and joined by planks, and about two hundred people live on them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Breakers' Yard
pointsOfInterest.description: Takes ships apart and sells them by the piece, which is most of the town's economy.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salvage Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Works nothing but recovered iron, and there is a great deal of recovered iron.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Chandlery
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything a ship needs, all of it off another ship.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salvage Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Sorted by what it came off rather than what it is, which makes perfect sense to everybody here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wet Locker
pointsOfInterest.description: Rot, damp, salt sores, and the things a long voyage does.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pilots' Shed
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven people who know the Narrows, and the Narrows change, and so does the eleven.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ship's Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Lifted whole out of a wreck, roof and all, and set down here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bilge
pointsOfInterest.description: Below the waterline of a ship that is on dry land, which is a distinction the landlord enjoys.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sternpost Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Four houses out of one ship, and you can see where the joins were.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pilot's Berth
pointsOfInterest.description: Best view of the Narrows in the town and the only one anybody wants.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Jetty
pointsOfInterest.description: One jetty, and everything that has ever happened here has happened on it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shag
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, one barrel, eleven families, and no strangers most years.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Rock Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Line, hooks, salt, and lamp oil.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Rock Chapel
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut into the rock rather than built on it, because of the wind.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old House
pointsOfInterest.description: Older than Blackrigging, and the family will tell you by how much.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ledge Cottages
pointsOfInterest.description: Three, on a ledge, with the sea forty feet below the doorstep.

pointsOfInterest.name: Halfmast Fort
pointsOfInterest.description: The sea got into it in 'sixty-three and it is still the best building on the island.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Half Mast
pointsOfInterest.description: There is one, in the yard, cut off at about twelve feet, and nobody will say why it was cut.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fort Store
pointsOfInterest.description: In the old magazine, which is the only dry room on the island.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gun Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Was a gun forge. Is now a forge.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gunner's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Built into the rampart, and the rampart does most of the work.

pointsOfInterest.name: Casemate Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Four families living in gun positions, and it is warmer than it sounds.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Passage
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven miles of shoal that moves between one season and the next, and it is the only way in.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pilot Station
pointsOfInterest.description: A hut on a rock with a flagstaff, and somebody in it whenever anything is expected.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Marker
pointsOfInterest.description: A ship set deliberately on the shoal to mark it, forty years ago, and she is still where she was put.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wreck Reef
pointsOfInterest.description: Three miles long, with about sixty ships on it in every stage of going, and the newest is four years old.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Salvors' Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: On the one dry rock, occupied whenever the weather allows, which is not often.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Wreck
pointsOfInterest.description: A ship on her side in the lee of the reef with her holds intact and her decks above water at low springs.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Gullstone Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: Four hundred feet of cut steps up a rock, no rail, and the wind never stops.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Top
pointsOfInterest.description: Flat, about an acre, forty thousand birds, and one building that nobody in the isles claims.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chimney
pointsOfInterest.description: A shaft through the middle of the rock from the top to the waterline, and the stair on the outside was cut to reach it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fort Hatch
pointsOfInterest.description: Open for about forty minutes either side of low water, and shut with the whole Iron Sea on top of it the rest of the time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drowned Walls
pointsOfInterest.description: Twelve feet of water over them at low tide and forty at high, and the parapet shows twice a day.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sea Battery
pointsOfInterest.description: Nine guns still in their positions, under water, pointing at a channel that has moved.

pointsOfInterest.name: Tern Bank
pointsOfInterest.description: Three miles of shingle that is a bank for nine months and a shoal for three.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bank Hut
pointsOfInterest.description: Rebuilt every spring, because it is under water every winter.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Bank Cut
pointsOfInterest.description: A winter storm cut the bank through and exposed something that had been under it, and the bank has not closed up again.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fungus Market
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven kinds of light, forty kinds of food, and all of it grown within two miles of here.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Lantern
pointsOfInterest.description: Hung from the roof of the cavern on a chain nobody can account for, and it has never been lit by anybody living.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lamp Shop
pointsOfInterest.description: Oil, wick, flint, and the only thing anybody here actually needs.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Stores
pointsOfInterest.description: Everything from above, at the price of having carried it down.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Deep Forge
pointsOfInterest.description: Vented up a shaft that somebody found rather than cut.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Rope Walk
pointsOfInterest.description: In a gallery a quarter of a mile long, which is exactly why the gallery was chosen.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wayfinders' Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty people who can get you from here to Karn Dolur and back, and the number who can is not increasing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shrine of the Second Light
pointsOfInterest.description: A lamp kept burning against the day the Great Lantern is lit, which the shrine maintains is coming.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Wick
pointsOfInterest.description: Beds, food, and a lamp on every table because the alternative is unbearable.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Second Terrace
pointsOfInterest.description: Cut into the cavern wall, forty feet up, reached by a stair everybody complains about.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Fungus Row
pointsOfInterest.description: Roofed in living fungus, which glows, which the residents say is free light and everybody else says is a fire risk in reverse.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Lower Workings
pointsOfInterest.description: The town has been quarrying its own cavern larger for four hundred years and the workings go further than the plan admits.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Growing Beds
pointsOfInterest.description: Eleven acres of fungus in terraces, fed on what Lantern Deep produces, which is a subject nobody dwells on.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Cap
pointsOfInterest.description: One room, and everything on the menu was grown within a hundred yards.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Spore Store
pointsOfInterest.description: Cultures, spawn, and the tools for handling both.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Drying House
pointsOfInterest.description: Warm, dry, and it is the only place in the Deeproads that is either.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Grower's House
pointsOfInterest.description: Built into the terrace wall, and it is warmer than it should be.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Spore Rooms
pointsOfInterest.description: Lodging for the growers, and everything in it is very slightly luminous.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Long Hall
pointsOfInterest.description: Four miles of dressed corridor forty feet wide, dead straight, with a ceiling nobody has surveyed.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Side Doors
pointsOfInterest.description: Two hundred and eleven of them down both walls, all the same size, and about nine of them open.

pointsOfInterest.name: Behind the Ninth Door
pointsOfInterest.description: The ninth door on the left is open, and everything behind it is laid out on the same plan as everything behind the other two hundred and ten.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Road Lamps
pointsOfInterest.description: Every two hundred paces, filled by somebody from Lantern Deep, and the filling is a job with a rota and a salary.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Road Station
pointsOfInterest.description: Halfway to the Long Hall, staffed, and the only reliably safe place on the road.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Toll
pointsOfInterest.description: Somebody charged for this road once, and the arch is still standing and the gate is not.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Canopy
pointsOfInterest.description: Forty feet up, a mile across, and bright enough underneath it to read by.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Pickers' Camp
pointsOfInterest.description: Wild-picked rather than farmed, which is worth more and is considerably worse for you.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Rot
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the canopy has come down and the floor beneath it has been eaten out from underneath.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Crossing
pointsOfInterest.description: A boat, a rope, and nobody to work either, and there has not been for some time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Sunless River
pointsOfInterest.description: Sixty feet wide, no sound whatsoever, and it has been going the same way for a very long time.

pointsOfInterest.name: Downstream
pointsOfInterest.description: It goes somewhere. Following it is the only way to find out and nobody has come back to say.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Black Bridge
pointsOfInterest.description: A single span over a chasm of no measured depth, with no parapet and no supports anybody can see.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Chasm
pointsOfInterest.description: You can drop a lamp down it and watch it for a very long time.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Footings
pointsOfInterest.description: There are chambers at both ends of the bridge, below the road level, and the bridge grows out of them.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Eleventh Chamber
pointsOfInterest.description: It will not let a word through, and until something is said correctly the far door does not open.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Ten Chambers
pointsOfInterest.description: A word comes back four times in each of them, each from a different direction, and none of them from the wall.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Listening Room
pointsOfInterest.description: Off the seventh chamber, and in it there is no echo at all, which is worse.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Broken Stair
pointsOfInterest.description: A hundred feet wide, going up towards the Ember Reach, with about a third of it missing.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Great Landing
pointsOfInterest.description: Halfway up, an acre of flat floor with the bases of columns on it and nothing above them.

pointsOfInterest.name: Beneath the Treads
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the stair has gone, you can see that it was hollow, and that there are rooms in the thickness of it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Weeping Roof
pointsOfInterest.description: Water through the roof in ten thousand places, and it has been doing it long enough to build the floor up to meet it.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Tarn Shaft
pointsOfInterest.description: The way up to the Weeping Moor, square-cut, and the rungs are rusted through for the top thirty feet.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Columns
pointsOfInterest.description: Where the drip has met the floor it has built columns, and eleven of them are hollow, and one of them has a door.

gates.name: The King's Gate
gates.description: Two towers, a portcullis nobody has dropped in thirty years, and a clerk with a ledger who will absolutely take your five marks.

gates.name: The River Gate
gates.description: Where the wall meets the water. The wharfingers pay by the year; everyone else pays at the arch.

gates.name: The Undercroft Door
gates.description: Iron-banded oak at the bottom of a stair nobody sweeps.

gates.name: The Pennyford Sluice
gates.description: The old ford gate. Shut, the channel runs deep and fast; open, it runs deeper and faster.

gates.name: The Landward Gate
gates.description: Sarnport charges to leave as well as to arrive, which the corporation describes as a road levy and nobody else does.

gates.name: The Battery Door
gates.description: A magazine door, iron on oak, with the corporation's seal across the keyhole.

gates.name: The Cliff Path
gates.description: Two feet wide with four hundred below it, and the last winter took some of the two feet.

gates.name: The Thornward
gates.description: A line of thorn laid across the ride, and it was laid across the ride, which thorn does not do by itself.

gates.name: The Moot Door
gates.description: The door in the oak. It is a door, in an oak, and it has hinges.

gates.name: The Pass Ward
gates.description: A wall across the pass with a gate in it, and the gate is shut whenever the wind is from the north, which is most of the time.

gates.name: The Hold Gate
gates.description: Forty tons of stone on a counterweight, and a gate-fee that the hold has charged since it was cut.

gates.name: The Deep Door
gates.description: The door to the abandoned levels, sealed by the hold and marked so in four languages.

requires.description: a hold-warrant for the deep levels

gates.name: The Ice Road
gates.description: The way north off the Cold Shoulder, over a snow bridge that is there in Deepdark and is not there in Longlight.

gates.name: The North Passage
gates.description: The sea road round the top of the continent, open for about nine weeks a year and not always those.

requires.description: a hull and a crew that have done it before

gates.name: The Cairn Ward
gates.description: Eleven hundred cairns, and a gap through them that is not the shortest way and is the only way anybody walks.

gates.name: The Keep Door
gates.description: The keep's own door, and the keep is standing on the barrow, and the two facts are related.

gates.name: The Sisters' Ward
gates.description: Nothing across the gap between the two southern stones, and you can walk it, and you very much do not want to.

requires.description: the words cut on the fallen stone

gates.name: The Tarn Shaft
gates.description: A shaft beside the Black Tarn, cut square, with the rungs rusted through for the first thirty feet.

gates.name: The Vent Ward
gates.description: A line of iron posts across the vent fields with a chain between them, and past the chain the ground is on its own schedule.

requires.description: a vent-reader's word on the day

gates.name: The Slag Door
gates.description: Cast in one piece, in place, by pouring it — which means it has never been opened and was never meant to be.

gates.name: The Pole Ferry
gates.description: A flat-bottomed punt and a man with a pole, and there is no other way across the Black Water in one day.

gates.name: The Belfry Hatch
gates.description: In the floor of the new bell tower, over the old one, and the village keeps it shut.

gates.name: The Passage
gates.description: The run out west through the shoals to the Sundered Isles, and nobody attempts it without somebody who has done it.

requires.description: passage money and a pilot who knows the shoals

gates.name: The Kurgan Ward
gates.description: No wall and no gate. A line of horse skulls on poles, and the riders will not cross it, and they will explain why at length and you will not be reassured.

requires.description: a khan's word, or a very good reason

gates.name: The Grazing Right
gates.description: Nobody owns the steppe. Everybody owns the grazing, and crossing somebody's grazing in season costs.

gates.name: The Water Gate
gates.description: Vashta Qal does not charge to enter. It charges to drink, at the gate, in advance, per head.

gates.name: The Bath Door
gates.description: Bronze, green, and it has been shut since the level dropped.

gates.name: The Crater Lip
gates.description: Nothing across it. The glass simply gets thin, and the thin part is over something.

gates.name: The Fort Hatch
gates.description: The way down into the drowned fort, and it is open for about forty minutes either side of low water.

requires.description: a tide table and the nerve to trust it

gates.name: The Gullstone Stair
gates.description: Four hundred feet of cut steps up a rock, with no rail, in a place where the wind does not stop.

gates.name: The Deep Gate
gates.description: Karn Dolur's door onto the Deeproads, and the hold charges more to go down than it does to come in.

gates.name: The Ferry of the Sunless River
gates.description: There is a boat. There is a rope. There is nobody to work either and there has not been for some time.

gates.name: The Echo Ward
gates.description: The eleventh chamber will not let a word through, and until something is said correctly the far door does not open.

requires.description: the phrase cut over the tenth door

dungeons.name: The Dene Barrow
dungeons.description: A long barrow above Hollowdene: an entrance passage, side cists, and a chamber at the end that the whole mound was raised over.

dungeons.name: The Hedge Setts
dungeons.description: Badger workings that go on rather too long and end in something that was cut with tools.

dungeons.name: The Roadstone Galleries
dungeons.description: Galleries driven into the quarry face when the open work stopped paying, and abandoned when the water came in.

dungeons.name: The Aurenhal Undercity
dungeons.description: The city's drains, and beneath them the streets they were cut through — three centuries of Aurenhal built on top of itself.

dungeons.name: The Warren Cellars
dungeons.description: Cellar under cellar under cellar, connected by people who did not want the connections known about.

dungeons.name: The Kingshold Undercroft
dungeons.description: Storerooms, and past the storerooms the river-fort the castle was built on, which nobody has surveyed past the fourth room.

dungeons.name: The Chalk Workings
dungeons.description: Quarried out from under the Rise to build the town, in pillar and stall, and the pillars are not all still there.

dungeons.name: The Flint Mines
dungeons.description: Shafts and galleries sunk for flint before iron, and worked with antler picks that are still lying where they were put down.

dungeons.name: The Smugglers' Run
dungeons.description: A sea cave at one end, a hole in a sheep field at the other, and a great deal of deliberate confusion in between.

dungeons.name: The Gannet Sea Caves
dungeons.description: Cut by the sea into the foot of the head. The front half floods twice a day and the back half has not in living memory.

dungeons.name: The Hollow Way
dungeons.description: The road before the road, sunk twenty feet and roofed over by growth, with side-chambers cut into the banks.

dungeons.name: The Root Cellar
dungeons.description: Dressed stone under the Beech King's roots, and the roots have been getting in for a century.

dungeons.name: The Deadfall
dungeons.description: A slip took the hillside off a doorway that was meant to stay shut, and what is behind it is not a cave.

dungeons.name: The Ride Barrow
dungeons.description: A long barrow astride the Greenway, and the Greenway goes round it, which settles the question of which came first.

dungeons.name: Under the Ring
dungeons.description: A stair inside the Ring going down into work that is not stone laid on stone but stone that was grown.

dungeons.name: The Deeps of Karn Dolur
dungeons.description: The levels the hold gave up: eleven tiers of hall and gallery, sealed at the top and not, apparently, at the bottom.

dungeons.name: The Old Seams
dungeons.description: Worked out four centuries back and left open, because a hold does not fill in what it might want again.

dungeons.name: The Ward Cellars
dungeons.description: Magazine, gaol, and store below the wall — and below those, chambers the wall was built on top of.

dungeons.name: The Cut Galleries
dungeons.description: Galleries running off the Cut, going a great deal further than the stone taken out of it could possibly account for.

dungeons.name: The Wind Cave
dungeons.description: Breathes out at dawn and in at dusk, which means it connects to something with a great deal of air in it.

dungeons.name: The Sink
dungeons.description: Follows the Weirwater into the mountain. Two miles have been surveyed. The third took the surveyor.

dungeons.name: Under the First Cairn
dungeons.description: The oldest cairn on the hill, opened once, and the keepers have not opened another since.

dungeons.name: The Blue Caves
dungeons.description: Melt channels in the calving face, which are a different shape every year and connect to different things.

dungeons.name: The Ribcage
dungeons.description: Built into the ribs of the largest whale on the strand, and then downward from there, by somebody with a plan.

dungeons.name: The Moulin
dungeons.description: A shaft drilled straight down through the glacier by meltwater, and dry from Rimewatch to Turning.

dungeons.name: Under the Pavement
dungeons.description: Whatever was quarried out from under the flats, opened again by wind taking the ice off the top of it.

dungeons.name: The Hollow
dungeons.description: The Last Cairn is standing on something, and the something is considerably larger than the cairn.

dungeons.name: Under Barrowgate Keep
dungeons.description: The keep's cellars, and then the barrow they were cut into, which the builders swore in writing they would not do.

dungeons.name: The Deep Cutting
dungeons.description: Eleven feet down through peat, a floor, and rooms under the floor, all of them wet.

dungeons.name: The Grit Caves
dungeons.description: Slots left where blocks came away from the edge, and one of them goes back into the hill and keeps going.

dungeons.name: Beneath the Sisters
dungeons.description: A cut stair between the eastern stones, and chambers under the ring laid out to the same plan as the ring.

dungeons.name: The Long Barrow
dungeons.description: Four hundred yards of grave: an entrance passage and forty cists off it, and a chamber at the west end.

dungeons.name: The Tarn Shaft
dungeons.description: A cut shaft beside the tarn going down to galleries that are on the Deeproads' plan, not the moor's.

dungeons.name: Under the Slag Cathedral
dungeons.description: The cathedral was cast on top of this, in one piece, over eleven years, with the door already shut.

dungeons.name: The Lava Tube
dungeons.description: A flow drained out from under its own crust: twenty feet across, round, and going a long way in.

dungeons.name: The Buried Village
dungeons.description: A street under eight feet of ash, entered through a chimney, with every door on it still shut.

dungeons.name: The Glass Stair
dungeons.description: A cut stair going down through a mile of obsidian, and the cutting is older than the glass.

dungeons.name: The Old Workings
dungeons.description: Iron got here before the reach caught fire, and abandoned in the middle of a shift with the tools where they fell.

dungeons.name: The Throat
dungeons.description: Down the inside of the Great Vent on ledges, in the nine hours between one eruption and the next.

dungeons.name: The Signal Deep
dungeons.description: A shaft under the seventh tower that the tower was put on top of on purpose, and it goes considerably further than the ridge.

dungeons.name: The Old Church
dungeons.description: Under the new bell tower, past the old bell, into a nave that has been under water two hundred years and is not full.

dungeons.name: The Sunken Hall
dungeons.description: A roof-ridge above the water, a hall below it, and below the hall a floor that is somehow dry.

dungeons.name: The Cypress Mound
dungeons.description: A rise in the middle of the maze that is not a natural rise, and the way in was cut, not washed.

dungeons.name: The Deep Hummock
dungeons.description: The one hummock made of stone rather than silt, and a stair through it going down under the water table.

dungeons.name: The Dry Well
dungeons.description: The fourth well, which nobody counts, dry for two hundred years, and with a dressed doorway at the bottom of it.

dungeons.name: The Great Kurgan
dungeons.description: The largest mound, at the head of the middle row, and the only one of the two hundred with a way in.

dungeons.name: The Cut Bank
dungeons.description: A flood took a bite out of the river bank and opened a stair that had been buried in it.

dungeons.name: The Sand Shaft
dungeons.description: Sand pours into it continuously and it has never filled, which means it is going somewhere.

dungeons.name: The Crater Deep
dungeons.description: A stair cut down the inside of the lip, in glass, going below the floor of the crater and continuing.

dungeons.name: The Deep Pan
dungeons.description: They cut down through the salt for better grade and came out of the bottom of it into a finished room.

dungeons.name: The Feeder
dungeons.description: The channel that fills the cistern, walked upstream in the nine years out of ten when that is possible.

dungeons.name: The Milepost Vault
dungeons.description: One milepost on the sunken road is hollow, and there is a stair in it, and it does not stop at the road's level.

dungeons.name: Under the Uncovered Town
dungeons.description: The dune moved off it eleven years ago; the cellars are intact because sand turns out to be an excellent roof.

dungeons.name: The Centre Shaft
dungeons.description: Straight down from the middle of the crater, glass-walled the whole way, and whatever made the crater went out this way.

dungeons.name: The Root
dungeons.description: A fulgurite that went down instead of up, wide enough to enter, and widened since by hands.

dungeons.name: The Ninth Well
dungeons.description: The only one of the eleven with rungs, and the rungs go down further than the shaft was ever dug.

dungeons.name: The Deep Wreck
dungeons.description: A great ship on her side in the lee of the reef, holds intact, decks above water at low springs and not otherwise.

dungeons.name: The Gullstone Chimney
dungeons.description: A shaft through the middle of the rock from the top to the waterline, and the stair outside was cut in order to reach it.

dungeons.name: The Drowned Fort
dungeons.description: Three levels of casemate, magazine, and cistern under a shoal, reachable for forty minutes either side of low water.

dungeons.name: The Bank Cut
dungeons.description: A winter storm cut the shingle through and exposed what was under it, and the bank has not closed since.

dungeons.name: The Lower Workings
dungeons.description: Four hundred years of Lantern Deep quarrying its own cavern larger, and it goes further than the plan admits.

dungeons.name: Behind the Ninth Door
dungeons.description: The ninth door on the left of the Long Hall, and everything behind it laid out on the same plan as the other two hundred and ten.

dungeons.name: The Rot
dungeons.description: Where the fungus canopy came down and the floor beneath it was eaten out from underneath.

dungeons.name: Downstream
dungeons.description: The Sunless River goes somewhere. Following it is the only way to find out and nobody has come back to say.

dungeons.name: The Footings
dungeons.description: Chambers at both ends of the Black Bridge, below road level, and the bridge grows out of them rather than resting on them.

dungeons.name: The Listening Room
dungeons.description: Off the seventh chamber of the Echo Halls, and in it there is no echo at all, which is worse.

dungeons.name: Beneath the Treads
dungeons.description: The Broken Stair is hollow, and where it has gone you can see there are rooms in the thickness of it.

dungeons.name: The Columns
dungeons.description: Eleven of the flowstone columns in the Weeping Vault are hollow, and one of them has a door in it.

variants.text: Scree shifts somewhere above you and takes a while to stop.
The air is thin enough that the climb costs more than it looks like it should.
Wind comes down the pass in one direction only, and hard.
Someone cut steps into this rock, and then nobody used them for a century.
Cloud comes over the ridge and the temperature goes with it.
Laid nine generations back, never once let through, and now a mile of thorn thick enough to lean on.
The Long Hedge goes where it wants and takes the lane with it.
You could get over it with a ladder and nobody in Ashcott would forgive you.
Roofs above the ash in a line, and everything below the roofs exactly as it was left in a hurry.
You go in through a chimney. There is a street down there.
The ash arrived over about four hours. There was time. Most of them took it.

Hollowdene, an hour after dawn, in the second week of Greening. The green is wet, the well is cold, and the road out of the village goes two ways: east to Aurenhal and the Kingsroad, or west into the hedges and whatever is past them. Nobody here has asked you for anything. That is the last time that will be true.

You come down onto Hollowdene green with the whole of the Kingsvale ahead of you and no particular reason to be in it. There is a well, an inn called the Ploughshare, a smithy going, and a barrow up the sheep field that everyone has told you to leave alone. The continent is considerably larger than this. It starts here anyway.

Morning in Hollowdene. Eleven roofs, one bell, and a road. Aurenhal is a day east, the coast is a week west, and the ice is further north than anybody sensible goes. You have boots, forty marks, and the entire Kingsvale to be wrong about first.
One long street of chimneys. Somebody laid this district out around the fire risk and the fire risk won.
Craftrow, and you can hear it before you turn into it: hammers on three different notes and somebody's grinding wheel under all of them.
Soot on the render, sparks going up somewhere behind the roofline, and every shopfront open to the street.
The trades that need heat, gathered where the wind takes it away from the rest of the city.
Four floors of shelving round a well of open air, with a lantern roof letting in the only light anybody trusts near the books.
The Grand Library, and a whispering that is entirely staff.
Ladders on rails, chained volumes on the second gallery, and a locked door on the fourth that everyone has a theory about.
The oldest roof in Aurenhal, and the fire of 'eighty-one went round it on both sides, which the priesthood has never once let anybody forget.
Pillars going up into dark, and a single light on the altar that is somebody's whole job.
Cold stone, deep quiet, and six hundred years of feet wearing a channel up the centre aisle.
The upper city, and it never lets you forget which way is up: the Kingshold on its rock, the Library's four floors of window, and stairs wherever a street would rather not climb.
Highgate. Clean paving, clipped hedges, and the particular hush of a district where most of the doors are somebody's office.
The Kingsroad arrives here and immediately becomes a formal avenue, which tells you most of what Highgate thinks about itself.
Above the smoke, mostly. On a clear day you can see the Weirwater going out west between the hedges.
The clerk does not look up. "Five marks the party, or the ledger, and the ledger takes longer."
A halberd comes down across the arch, unhurriedly. "Toll."
"Five marks," says the gate-clerk, "and before you ask, yes, everyone."
A castle that started as a river-fort and has been argued with by every monarch since: four periods of wall, three of roof, and one staircase that goes nowhere because somebody died mid-project.
The Kingshold. The curtain wall is honest defensive work; everything inside it is somebody making a point.
Guards on the gate who have been told to look bored and are managing it easily. Above them, banners, and above those, jackdaws.
Storerooms under the keep: barrels, ledgers, cold. And past the storerooms, a doorway cut in a wall that predates the castle by three hundred years.
The undercroft goes back further than the plans do. Somebody surveyed to the fourth room and then the survey stops.
Down, and then down again. The air changes at the second landing and does not change back.
Where marks come from: two doors, both watched, and a courtyard between them that you cross alone.
The Mint. Nothing about the building is decorative and everything about it is expensive.
You can hear the presses from the street, which is presumably the intention.
"Three marks or a wharfinger's chit," says the man on the arch, "and you have not got a chit."
The chain across the water gate stays where it is. Somebody points at a board with a number on it.
"Wharf dues," says the collector, already holding out a hand.
Wharf, warehouse, wharf, warehouse, and the Weirwater going past all of it at a speed the city finds convenient.
Riverside. Cranes, cranes, and men standing about waiting for a tide that does not come this far up.
The smell is river, tar, and fish in that order, and it changes with the wind but never entirely.
Half the district is built on piles and the other half wishes it were.
The Warrens are older than the wall that was put round them, and the wall has been losing the argument ever since.
Lanes that were never planned, going where the buildings let them. Two storeys overhead nearly touch.
Washing across the alley, a light in a shrine nobody admits to keeping, and about four hundred people who would rather you moved along.
It is not dangerous exactly. It simply has no interest in being legible to you.
The keep door is shut and the constable is not minded to open it for this.
"The cellars are the constable's business," says the man on the door, "and you are not."
Iron-strapped, barred inside, and a spyhole that opens and closes again.
Eleven feet wide, four hundred long, no parapet, no supports, and it does not flex under you at all.
The chasm underneath has never been sounded and several people have tried.
It grows out of the rock at both ends. It was not laid on anything.
Black, still, forty yards of it, and no line anybody has let down has found the bottom.
The surface does not move even when the heather is flattening.
The margin is bare mud for a yard all the way round, and nothing grows in it.
Forty acres of cypress that died standing, all in the same year, and nobody agrees which year.
Bare grey trunks out of black water, all of them still upright, none of them rotting.
Two hundred trees, and not one has fallen. Cypress does not do that.
Eleven ships moored in a row and joined by planks, and about two hundred people living aboard them.
The whole assembly rises and falls together, which is disconcerting for about a day.
Washing between the masts, smoke from eleven stove-pipes, and children going from ship to ship at a run.
A merchantman that came ashore stern-first in 'eighty-one and has been an inn ever since, in exactly the position she landed.
The Weatherly. The floors slope aft and everybody has stopped noticing.
The great cabin is the best room and it is let by the week.
Ribs the height of a house, in rows, going into the surf and out of it.
You can walk a quarter mile here without touching stone.
Some of the bones have been worked. Not recently. Not by anybody from the Landing.
Eleven shafts, dressed and lined, sunk at enormous cost, and dry every one.
The spoil heaps are still there beside them, undisturbed, which means nobody came back.
The ninth has rungs. The others do not. The rungs go further down than the shaft was dug.
A hundred feet wide, going up, and about a third of the treads are not there any more.
It is warm here and warmer further up, which tells you what it is going towards.
Where the treads have gone you can see straight into the thickness of the stair, and there are rooms in it.
Eleven hundred stone heaps on the hill, in rows, and the rows are not chronological.
The keepers know what every one is for. They will not tell you and they will not be rude about it.
You are asked to walk the marked way. The marked way is not the short way.
Shafts sunk thirty feet into the chalk, ringed with spoil, and grassed over so completely they look like dew ponds.
One of them is open. The others are not, and one of them was open last year.
They were sinking these for flint before anybody on this coast had seen iron.
Cut through the turf into the chalk, three hundred feet from nose to tail, and nobody can tell you who by.
The White Horse. Scoured every seventh year by everybody who lives within a day's walk, whether they want to or not.
From below it is a horse. From directly above, which nobody has ever been, it is presumably something else.
It was cast in place, shut, in one pour. There is no keyhole because there was never a key.
The Slag Door has no seam, no hinge, and no handle, and the cathedral was built over it afterwards.
Whatever this was meant to keep in, it was meant to keep in permanently.
Cast, not built. They poured it over eleven years and it has no joints anywhere in it.
The Slag Cathedral. The walls are one piece and so is the roof and so, unfortunately, is the door in the floor.
Black, seamless, and warm to the touch on the north side for reasons nobody has satisfactorily explained.
Gulls quarrel over something the tide left.
The sea works away at the chalk below, patient about it.
Salt has got into the grass and left it stiff and pale.
Wind off the water takes the words out of your mouth.
Far out, a sail leans over and is gone behind the headland.
Short turf over white rock, sheep to the horizon, and a horse cut into the hillside by somebody four thousand years ago.
The downs. No hedges, no trees, no shelter, and a view of about twenty miles.
Dry underfoot, springy, and the chalk shows white wherever a track has worn through.
Skylarks going up, one after another, all the way across.
A market cross, four streets, and more wheelwrights than a town this size can possibly need.
Cobbleway. Everything going to or from Sarnport stops here, and the town has arranged itself entirely around that.
Carts nose to tail in the market place, and the smell of hot iron from the tyring yard.
Stone-built and slate-roofed, and prosperous in an unshowy way.
Four hundred feet of chalk, forty thousand birds, and a noise you feel in your chest.
Gannet Head. The path along the top is narrower than it was and getting narrower.
White cliffs, white birds, white water at the bottom, and the smell of all three.
The whole headland is going into the sea, in its own time, about a foot a year.
Eleven boats up the shingle, a capstan for each, and forty people who are all related.
Gullmere. There is no harbour; there is a beach, and that has been enough for six hundred years.
Nets over every fence and a smell of tar you stop noticing after an hour.
The whole village faces the sea and turns its back on the downs.
Turf, flint cottages, and pink flowers over the cliff edge in every direction.
Thrift, which is the flower, though the villagers are happy to let you assume the other thing.
